water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: The only damage-type unit is an establishment-phase loss in Tunisia: drought caused a shortfall in the spate-irrigation and water-recharge works established in the governorate of Medenine, where only 15 were built against a target of 95 [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: This rests on a single ex-post review of project completion data and describes works that were never built, not damage to existing structures. Units about storage running dry or benefits shrinking in drought are effect units recording a benefit shortfall, not damage, and practitioner coping ratings are not counted here, so no unit in this row measures structural damage to built works.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Storms overtop, breach or collapse works: storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau, with few local funds to repair it, staggered earth bunds (tabia) in Morocco store the runoff of rains below 50 mm, but in the biggest storms the excess overtops the bunds and gullies the slope, tied ridges in a Kenyan trial collapsed in heavy rainfall events and had to be rebuilt within the season, and poorly structured vineyard terraces in Spain suffered severe landslides after a single rainstorm [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7, ev_climate_shock_roos10_1_av, ev_climate_shock_ndun23_1_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av]. In Algeria a poorly maintained banquette network fails in a chain reaction during torrential and prolonged rains, the smallest unrepaired breach spreading sliding through the whole network [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av], and a check-dam review links failures worldwide to extreme rainfall events or lack of maintenance [ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av]. WOCAT compilers judge zaï pits, contour stone bunds, semi-circular bunds, contour bunds and Vallerani trenches in Niger, radical terraces in Rwanda, stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde, gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and ripper tillage in Zambia not to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1219_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1616_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1614_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1652_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1613_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1493_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1139_2013_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Compilers for jessour and gabion check dams in Tunisia, check dams and bench terraces in China, sand dams in Kenya, spate irrigation in Eritrea, stone-covered bench terraces in Yemen and vetiver-hedge terraces in Haiti judge them to cope well with rainstorms, and those for terraces in Thailand and Bangladesh and marab and Vallerani systems in Jordan to cope very well [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1013_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1400_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1455_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1537_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_3223_2017_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4281_2018_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5770_2020_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5860_2021_local_rainstorm]; weirs in Ethiopia, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia and the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso are rated as coping moderately [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6715_2023_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_7778_2026_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1528_2012_local_rainstorm]. The literature ties damage to upkeep and construction quality: the Algerian failures concern poorly maintained banquettes, the Spanish landslides poorly structured terraces, and the check-dam failures lack of maintenance as well as extreme rain [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av, ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av]. Most units are compiler ratings or manual and review statements rather than damage records, the only field observation is from a single Kenyan trial, and for field-level practices (pits, bunds, ripper tillage) a not-well rating describes exposure of fields rather than damage to a structure [ev_climate_shock_ndun23_1_av, ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: In Algeria a poorly maintained banquette network fails in a chain reaction during torrential and prolonged rains, the smallest unrepaired breach spreading sliding through the whole network [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av]. In Morocco staggered earth bunds (tabia) in Morocco store the runoff of rains below 50 mm, but in the biggest storms the excess overtops the bunds and gullies the slope [ev_climate_shock_roos10_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Both are expert or survey statements without damage counts; the Algerian failure is explicitly tied to poor maintenance, and the Moroccan statement implies the bunds hold for ordinary rains and fail only in the largest storms [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av, ev_climate_shock_roos10_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau with few local funds to repair it, and WOCAT compilers judge pits, bunds and trenches in Niger, radical terraces in Rwanda, gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and ripper tillage in Zambia not to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1219_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1493_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1139_2013_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Other compilers in Tunisia, Eritrea, Kenya, Yemen, Uganda, India, Madagascar and Ethiopia judge coping as good, and those in Burkina Faso, Bangladesh and Somalia as moderate; the Haiti and Bangladesh terrace sheets judge coping with landslides as very good [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1013_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1537_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_7778_2026_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_3223_2017_landslide]. All units except the Loess Plateau observation are practitioner judgements without damage records, and for field-level practices a not-well rating describes exposure of fields rather than damage to a structure.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the WOCAT compiler for stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde judges them not to cope well with local rainstorms, and in Algeria a poorly maintained banquette network fails in a chain reaction during torrential and prolonged rains, the smallest unrepaired breach spreading sliding through the whole network [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Compilers judge check dams and progressive bench terraces in China to cope well, and a continuous bench terrace for tea in Thailand and the marab and Vallerani systems in Jordan to cope very well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1455_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1522_2010_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4281_2018_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5770_2020_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5860_2021_local_rainstorm]. The units are compiler ratings and a secondary statement from an Algerian evaluation that links the failure to poor maintenance, not measurements of damage [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate bench terraces in Bangladesh as coping moderately with forest fire and well with land fire, and stone check walls and check dams in India as coping well with forest fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_forest_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_land_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_5210_2019_forest_fire].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings from two technology sheets with no observed damage; earth and stone works offer little to burn, so any fire effect would fall on vegetation on or around them.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Intense runoff overwhelms or breaks structures: floods washed away scores of small dams in northern Ghana, 37.9% of boulder-faced log check dams in Ethiopia failed after a high-magnitude runoff event, check-dam failure releases stored sediment, large floods could wash out traditional spate diversions in Yemen, banquettes lack capacity for erosive rains and overflow, and torrential rain collapses terrace walls or carries small terraces away in mass movements [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. A check-dam review cites structural failure from the impact of large boulders in extreme floods, and grassed earth gully check dams in Morocco are described as fragile during major floods and needing frequent winter maintenance [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1_av, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av]. WOCAT compilers judge jessour in Tunisia, zaï pits, bunds and trenches in Niger, the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso, check dam ponds in Ethiopia, radical terraces in Rwanda, gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and ripper tillage in Zambia not to cope well with river or flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1013_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1616_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1528_2012_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1547_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1493_2011_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Other compilers judge sand dams in Kenya, check dams in Tunisia, China and India, and spate or water-spreading systems in Eritrea and Sudan to cope well, those for marab and Vallerani systems in Jordan and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia to cope very well, and those for weirs in Ethiopia and works in Somalia to cope moderately [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1537_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6716_2023_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7777_2026_flash_flood]; these are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, and for field-level practices (pits, bunds, tillage) a not-well rating describes exposure of fields to floodwater rather than damage to a structure. Literature failures are tied to maintenance and design: rarely maintained diversion systems generally fail after 4 to 10 years, terrace collapse is linked to abandonment, the Rwandan mass movement happened on terraces without trees, and the Moroccan earth check dams need frequent upkeep [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av]. The boulder-impact and sediment-release statements are secondary citations or come from a USA study, and the Yemen statement refers to diversions before project improvements [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1_av, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Intense runoff overwhelms or breaks structures: floods washed away scores of small dams in northern Ghana, 37.9% of boulder-faced log check dams in Ethiopia failed after a high-magnitude runoff event, large floods could wash out traditional spate diversions in Yemen, banquettes in Niger lack capacity for erosive rains and overflow, in Rwanda a very rainy week can carry away all the small terraces on a slope without trees in a mass movement, and grassed earth gully check dams in Morocco are fragile during major floods [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av]. WOCAT compilers judge jessour in Tunisia, zaï pits, bunds and Nardi/Vallerani trenches in Niger, the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso, check dam ponds in Ethiopia, radical terraces in Rwanda, gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and ripper tillage in Zambia not to cope well with river or flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1013_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1219_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1613_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1528_2012_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1547_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1553_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1493_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1139_2013_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Other compilers judge water spreading in Sudan, spate irrigation in Eritrea, a gabion check dam and stone lines in Tunisia, sand dams in Kenya, stone check walls and check dams in India and gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan to cope well, water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia and haffir and gabion works in Somalia to cope moderately, and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia to cope very well [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1292_2015_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1333_2010_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1400_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6610_2022_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1537_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5210_2019_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7553_2025_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6715_2023_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7777_2026_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7778_2026_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6716_2023_flash_flood]. Most units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets or manuals, not measurements, and for field-level practices (pits, bunds, tillage) a not-well rating describes exposure of fields to floodwater rather than damage to a structure; the Moroccan statement ties fragility to maintenance, the Yemen statement describes diversions before project improvements, and the Ethiopian log-dam failure rate is reported second-hand in a review [ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: A review of terraces names torrential rain, together with the collapse of walls and vegetation strips and use after abandonment, among the conditions that degrade terraces [ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3]. WOCAT compilers judge a check dam for land in China and stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde to cope well with river floods, and marab floodplain agriculture and mechanised Vallerani micro-catchments in Jordan to cope very well with flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1455_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1573_2013_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5860_2021_flash_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: The pool is small and, apart from the review, consists of practitioner judgements from documented technology sheets rather than measured damage; the review ties damage to abandonment as much as to rainfall. The Jordanian ratings carry no damage signal at all.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan rates the technology as coping very well with extreme winter conditions [ev_asset_frost_wocat_5860_2021_extreme_winter_conditions].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating from Jordan with no observed damage, so it says little about frost exposure elsewhere [ev_asset_frost_wocat_5860_2021_extreme_winter_conditions].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for gabions and rock check dams in Somalia rates the technology as coping moderately with heatwaves [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: This rests on a single practitioner rating with no stated reason or observed damage, for a structure of stone and wire that heat would affect mainly through the vegetation around it [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Slope failure damages terraces where slopes are unstable or terraces are abandoned: in the Tizi Ouzou region of Algeria 19% of banquettes on marls and clays were damaged by landslides and as many by gullying, and in Mediterranean regions over 50% of abandoned terraces were vulnerable to gully erosion and landslides that collapse the dry-stone walls [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av]. Among WOCAT compilers, stone check walls and check dams in India are rated as coping only moderately with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5210_2019_landslide].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Other compilers rate stone lines in Tunisia, a masonry check dam in Ethiopia and a continuous bench terrace for tea in Thailand as coping well, and vetiver-hedge bench terraces with trees in Haiti and bench terraces on hilly slopes in Bangladesh as coping very well [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6610_2022_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6716_2023_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4281_2018_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_3223_2017_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4284_2018_landslide]. The damage figures are secondary citations tied to marl and clay substrates and to abandonment, not to maintained terraces, and the ratings come from a small set of technology sheets rather than measurements [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Reservoirs, tanks and dams trap the sediment that runoff carries, so storage fills and function declines: Tigray dams with a 30-year design life were set to run their cycle in 4.4 to 5.7 years, eight of ten Zambian reservoirs lost storage to siltation, 31 percent of earthen dams in Haryana silted up within five years, Moroccan gabions had nearly lost their original function, and small hill dams in Morocco lose 0.5 to 1% of capacity each year to catchment erosion [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_1, ev_asset_siltation_saru19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_iegind11_12, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2, ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av]. Loose-rock check dams on semi-arid rangeland watersheds in the USA were filled to more than 80% of capacity within four years, and a review notes the sediment-control effect of check dams diminishes as they fill and becomes marginal a few years to a few decades after installation [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1_av]. Sedimentation is described as perhaps the primary reason for sand dam failure, and tanks desilted in an Indian programme need desilting again within its lifetime [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3, ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1]. On Ethiopian highland bunds, a filled drainage ditch quickly lowers sediment-trapping efficiency and adds pressure that can lead to structural failure [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1_av]. In Burkina Faso the 2- and 3-m half-moon plots showed lower infiltration than the control plots, likely due to suspended matter that clogs the soil during sedimentation [ev_soil_permeability_zour25h1_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Severity varies: a Kenyan sand-dam assessment estimates siltation cut storage by 10-25% and judges it neither an inherent limitation nor the main reason dams go unused [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. Most units are review citations or narrative observations without a common metric, the only directly measured fill rate comes from a high-income rangeland study, and losses depend on upkeep, as the Moroccan structures failed where no maintenance system had been put in place and small hill dams were forgotten once built [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_2, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2, ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av]. The half-moon clogging is a loss of infiltration in the larger basins, with a likely cause the authors name but do not test, not a structural failure [ev_soil_permeability_zour25h1_8].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: No unit describes how wind damages the works; the row rests on WOCAT compiler judgements of how terraces, bunds, pits, check dams, sand dams and spate systems cope with local windstorms and tropical storms. Most are judged to cope well, while progressive bench terraces in China and fascine vegetative check dams in Madagascar are judged not to cope well [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1522_2010_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_6478_2022_tropical_storm].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements from documented technology sheets, not measurements; compilers for bench terraces in Bangladesh and gabion works in Somalia judge coping as moderate, and the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso is judged to cope very well [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4284_2018_tropical_storm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_7778_2026_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1528_2012_local_windstorm]. For field-level practices such as pits and bunds a rating describes exposure of fields rather than damage to a structure.

water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.mechanism: In Burkina Faso the proximity of zai pits on bare, crusted land raises germination and seed dispersal, so herbaceous and woody species re-establish on formerly barren fields, and users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive greener surroundings and improved biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_roose93_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_zoug14_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_kabo04_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_veno12_1]. WOCAT compilers give a mechanism with each rating: water held by on-farm ponds in Cambodia lets plants grow, sand dams in Kenya rejuvenate riverine ecologies and enable indigenous tree planting, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia improve soil moisture, vegetation and habitat for livestock and small wildlife, and the Vallerani System in Burkina Faso brings more forage grasses, returning legumes and observed insects, birds, reptiles and mammals [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_2844_2017_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1537_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1528_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1528_2012_animal_diversity]. Embrapa reports that crops, vegetable gardens and orchards on the humid fringes of its barraginhas in Brazil bring back fauna that had disappeared for lack of food [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.conditionality: The WOCAT units are compiler ratings from documented technology sheets in Burkina Faso, Kenya, Cambodia, Somalia, Ethiopia, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Zambia, not measurements, and several sheets supply separate plant, animal and habitat ratings; the literature units are descriptive species counts or user perceptions with no untreated comparison, and the zai counts partly restate the same earlier observation. The Magoye ripper sheet in Zambia rates animal diversity unchanged, the Bangladesh bench-terrace rating is an expectation for a planned cropping system, and the Bhutan rating refers to more diverse crops [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1139_2013_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4284_2018_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity]. The barraginha fauna finding is an adopter-reported indicator in Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, and the gain comes through the gardens and orchards on the humid fringe rather than the basin itself [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.mechanism: Consecutive years of zai planting pits on formerly bare, barren soil in central Burkina Faso were followed by the re-establishment of herbaceous species and of trees and shrubs.
water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.conditionality: Both units are secondary citations of earlier zai field observations from Burkina Faso, probably overlapping, reporting species counts on treated land without an untreated comparison or a biodiversity index; the strength of the effect is not quantified.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: WOCAT compilers attribute carbon gains to more vegetation: the Vallerani System in Burkina Faso raises biomass production many times over nearby unploughed soil, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia increase biomass and, through vegetation recovery and sediment accumulation, soil organic matter, a haffir in Somalia allows vegetation cover to regenerate, gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan add below-ground organic matter through expanding roots, and the Magoye ripper in Zambia does so through less soil disturbance [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1528_2012_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7778_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7777_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7553_2025_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1139_2013_biomass_above_ground_C]. Emission ratings rest on tree nurseries enabled by sand dams in Kenya and tree cover building up over time at a masonry check dam in Ethiopia, and in the literature zai fields in Burkina Faso treated for several years had higher organic matter while trenches combined with vegetation raised soil organic carbon [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1537_2012_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_6716_2023_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_kabo04_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_1]. A check-dam review cites check dams on China's Loess Plateau contributing to carbon sequestration, an effect that grows with time at both dam and watershed level as sediment accumulates [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. A meta-analysis of Chinese soil and water conservation measures, available as a preprint, finds soil organic carbon 10.74% to 22.63% above the initial level after straw mulching across regions, and 3.36% and 75.77% higher after contour tillage in two regions within 5 to 10 years [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_4]. The same preprint meta-analysis finds terracing raised soil organic carbon by 27%, 17.94% and 26.62% in three Chinese regions, with increases of 14.11% to 60.96% in regional subsets 11 to 30 years after construction [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_5, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_6, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_7, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_9, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_11]. A Chinese meta-analysis, available as a preprint, reports fish-scale pits raising soil organic carbon storage by 79.86% on the Loess Plateau in years 11~30 [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_12]. In Burkina Faso, soils on farms using soil and water conservation techniques had higher carbon and nitrogen contents than the control farm [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3], and a review cites climate-smart packages of soil and water conservation structures with biological measures boosting soil carbon stock by three to seven times over business-as-usual [ev_soil_organic_carbon_tade23h1_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: Most units are compiler ratings from documented technology sheets in Niger, Uganda, Jordan, Tunisia, Sudan, Ethiopia, Rwanda, Haiti, Bangladesh, Bhutan and elsewhere, not measurements, many soil organic matter ratings carry no comment, and soil organic matter and emission ratings are proxies rather than measured sequestration; the Bangladesh emission rationale (crops absorbing more carbon dioxide under higher cropping intensity) is not long-term storage, and the Bhutan sheet describes organic matter moving downslope within each terrace [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_4284_2018_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_6891_2023_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C]. The literature is mixed: trenches in Mexico lowered soil nitrogen and carbon, and a zai trial in Burkina Faso found no significant change in organic matter by the end of the experiment even though biomass rose [ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_roose93_1]. The Loess Plateau check-dam finding is a secondary citation in a review, with no magnitude in the quoted passage [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. The Chinese figures come from a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, in an upper-middle-income country. Several are the values for the duration window with the greatest increase rather than a pooled estimate, and the duration subsets overlap the regional ones [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_12]. The Burkina Faso result is a carbon content on farm soils, not a stock change, and the three-to-sevenfold stock gain is a review's citation of a package that includes biological measures, very large for structures and to be read with caution [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_tade23h1_3]. Paired soil samples from Zambian fields under planting basins or ripping (bundled with reduced tillage), with crop residues hardly retained, showed no significant difference in organic carbon from conventional fields [ev_soil_organic_carbon_umar11_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: In low-income settings the pathway is zai pits building soil organic matter over time, with organic matter and nitrogen higher on fields treated for several years.
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: Both units are zai in Burkina Faso and measure soil organic matter, a proxy for carbon; one is a secondary citation of an earlier study and the other, a controlled trial, found no significant change in organic matter after two years.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for marab floodplain water harvesting and mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan rate soil organic matter increased, and a review of infiltration trenches reports that trenches combined with vegetation raised soil nutrients including soil organic carbon [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5770_2020_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5860_2021_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_1]. A check-dam review cites check dams on China's Loess Plateau contributing to carbon sequestration, an effect that grows with time at both dam and watershed level as sediment accumulates [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. A meta-analysis of Chinese soil and water conservation measures, available as a preprint, finds soil organic carbon 10.74% to 22.63% above the initial level after straw mulching across regions, and 3.36% and 75.77% higher after contour tillage in two regions within 5 to 10 years [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_4]. The same preprint meta-analysis finds terracing raised soil organic carbon by 27%, 17.94% and 26.62% in three Chinese regions, with increases of 14.11% to 60.96% in regional subsets 11 to 30 years after construction [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_5, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_6, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_7, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_9, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_11]. A Chinese meta-analysis, available as a preprint, reports fish-scale pits raising soil organic carbon storage by 79.86% on the Loess Plateau in years 11~30 [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_12].
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: The Jordanian ratings carry no compiler comment and are practitioner judgements, not measurements, with soil organic matter standing in for sequestration. The same review reports that trenches in Mexico actually decreased soil nitrogen and carbon, so the in-scope literature is split [ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_2]. The Loess Plateau check-dam result is a secondary citation without a magnitude in the quoted passage [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. The Chinese figures come from a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, in an upper-middle-income country. Several are the values for the duration window with the greatest increase rather than a pooled estimate, and the duration subsets overlap the regional ones [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_12]. In this scope the preprint carries most of the measured signal.

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: Groundwater recharge now counts as a component of catchment water yield, so this row holds two kinds of evidence. Most units report recharge and rising water tables at or near capture structures: the proportion of runoff infiltrated through check dams can reach more than 50%, with recharge linked to episodic storm events [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_luca21_1]; groundwater tables rise in the vicinity of filled check dams, and sand dams can raise the local groundwater [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_fran21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1]; in India additional recharge from check dams and other water harvesting structures was estimated at 480 million cubic meters per annum, groundwater levels rose in 16 of 21 non-desert districts with an average increase of 1.42 meters, and a state survey found levels increased in 22 of the 31 districts [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_3, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_2]; the Uttarakhand water budget shows aquifer recharge up 3.3 percent and water yield from catchment areas up 4.9 percent [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5], and ISRO survey data record increased recharge in treated areas [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3]; terraces would cause a groundwater recharge of 15 to 25% of rainfall, and modelling of contour ridges in Morocco estimates a 50% increase in recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1]; stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale increase ground water level, and in Burkina Faso improved well levels are linked to SWC measures that control surface runoff and improve infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]; communities in Mauritania, spate beneficiaries in Yemen and an Ethiopian public-works assessment report rising well levels, increased groundwater or water-table improvements [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mrt14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_2, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_eth16_7]; and a review lists aquifer recharge among benefits cited for water harvesting [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_saru19_1]. The two reductions are measured on flow leaving the treated land: On China's Loess Plateau, a large campaign of check-dam construction carried out since the 1970s to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments reduced streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1], and in the Maghreb mechanised bund systems, built with large machines that scrape a 4 to 10 m strip to raise bunds 1.5 to 2 m high every 30 to 50 m, considerably reduce the water collected in downstream hill reservoirs and cost 10 to 25% of the cultivable area [ev_water_yield_roos10_1]. In Burkina Faso, cited studies show soil and water conservation techniques improving the availability of ground water in many villages, especially large rock bunds known as digues filtrantes [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6]. Embrapa says its barraginhas in Brazil help recharge groundwater by raising the water table and revitalise springs and rivers [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. The two sides are measured in different places: the gains are groundwater and well levels at or near the structures, the losses are streamflow and reservoir inflow below large-scale works — a check-dam campaign built to retain floodwater and mechanised bunds. The class follows the sub-practice vote. The terracing row holds the strongest result, moderate positive, on the terrace recharge estimate and the Moroccan contour-ridge modelling [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1]. The runoff-catchment row (check dams, sand dams, small reservoirs) holds slight positive, because it carries the Loess Plateau streamflow reduction alongside its recharge reports [ev_water_yield_luca21_1], and the spate and cross-family rows also hold slight positive. The in-field row leans slightly negative: it holds the Maghreb mechanised-bund reduction and the Peruvian trench baseflow finding against the Mauritanian well levels and the Andean recharge that cannot be generalised [ev_water_yield_roos10_1, ev_water_regulation_locat20_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mrt14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1]. The weighted median of the positive rows is slight positive, below the pooled moderate. No unit compares downstream flow with and without the works, so the slight positive class says that capture recharges local aquifers, not that more water reaches users downstream. The recharge side has limits in its own sources: the sand-dam effect is often limited in space and time [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1]; in India, pumping from tube wells that land-owning farmers sank as the water table rose has possibly wiped out any increases in recharge from the watershed treatments, and without data from untreated sites the project impact is unclear [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3]; in Burkina Faso the number of wells with water year round has not increased significantly since SWC began [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]; and catchment-level recharge gains in the Andes are plausible but cannot be generalised [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1]. Most recharge units are secondary citations, programme reports or modelling, and few state a size, which caps the class. On the loss side, the 39% is a figure the check-dam review cites from another study (Shi et al., 2015) for one Chinese region [ev_water_yield_luca21_1], and the Maghreb reduction is a narrative from a Moroccan expert manual with no figure for the water lost downstream; the 10 to 25% is cultivable area, not water [ev_water_yield_roos10_1]. Against both, the downstream streamflow impacts of small-scale water storage systems have in other cases been limited, even when implemented widely [ev_water_yield_rock10_1], and trenches in the Peruvian Andes had little effect on increasing baseflow, with hydrogeological characteristics key to explaining their impact [ev_water_regulation_locat20_1]. The digues filtrantes finding is cited from another study, with no figures [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6]. The barraginha recharge statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measurement behind it [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: In the Sahel, stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale increase ground water level [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1], and in Burkina Faso levels of water in wells have improved, which the source links not to higher rainfall but to SWC measures that control surface runoff and improve infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]. On China's Loess Plateau, a large campaign of check-dam construction carried out since the 1970s to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments reduced streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. In Burkina Faso, cited studies show soil and water conservation techniques improving the availability of ground water in many villages, especially large rock bunds known as digues filtrantes [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: Both sides are real findings in semi-arid land, and what separates them is the outcome measured, the place and the scale of the works. The gain is groundwater and well levels on and around treated Sahelian fields and watersheds [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]; the loss is streamflow below a campaign of check dams built at very large scale in China to retain floodwater [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. For a downstream user the Chinese finding is the relevant one; for a farmer near the works the Sahelian one is. Neither side compares with and without the works at catchment scale: the Sahelian units are cited statements, the 39% is cited by a review from another study, and in Burkina Faso the number of wells with water year round has not increased significantly since SWC began [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]. The added Burkina Faso village groundwater finding sits on the gain side, is cited from another study and gives no figures [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: In the lower-income settings in this scope, mechanised bund systems, built with large machines that scrape a 4 to 10 m strip to raise bunds 1.5 to 2 m high every 30 to 50 m, considerably reduce the water collected in downstream hill reservoirs and cost 10 to 25% of the cultivable area [ev_water_yield_roos10_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. It rests on two units and neither carries a figure for downstream water: the reduction is a narrative from a Moroccan expert manual citing earlier work [ev_water_yield_roos10_1], and the counterweight is a review statement that the downstream streamflow impacts of small-scale water storage systems have in other cases been limited, even when implemented widely [ev_water_yield_rock10_1]. The two describe different works, large mechanised bunds against small-scale storage, so they do not directly contradict each other. Spring and stream discharge gains near treated watersheds are local supply and are reported in the water stress rows, not here.

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: Upstream capture can both add to and take from downstream water. On China's Loess Plateau, a large campaign of check-dam construction carried out since the 1970s to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments reduced streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. On the other side, Embrapa says its barraginhas in Brazil help recharge groundwater by raising the water table and revitalise springs and rivers [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6], and in the Peruvian Andes a few studies have observed catchment-level changes such as reduced quick runoff or increased aquifer recharge, which the source calls plausible but not generalisable [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. The sides now conflict, and what separates them is what is measured and at what scale: the loss is streamflow below a check-dam campaign at very large scale built to retain floodwater [ev_water_yield_luca21_1], while the gains are recharge and water-table statements for small dispersed basins and trenches [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1]. In the Peruvian Andes trenches had little effect on increasing baseflow, with hydrogeological characteristics key to explaining their impact [ev_water_regulation_locat20_1]. None of this is a measured project comparison: the 39% is a secondary citation in a global review, the Peruvian statements are a review's summary, and the barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology [ev_water_yield_luca21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.mechanism: In a Kenyan catchment, low-cost water measures built around sand dams are estimated to have given more than 100,000 people better access to water within 10 years at an investment of about 35 USD per capita [ev_project_cost_lasage08_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.conditionality: This is a single estimate from a single study, with no stated currency year, expressed per person gaining water access rather than per farmer or household, so it covers the water-access benefit only [ev_project_cost_lasage08_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.mechanism: Pooled costs are up-front establishment costs per hectare: compiler-reported establishment costs from WOCAT technology sheets for water-harvesting and conservation technologies in Ethiopia, India, Niger, Uganda, Tunisia, Yemen, Jordan, Uzbekistan, Somalia and Cabo Verde, plus watershed treatment costs per treated hectare from two India projects, the average investment cost of spate systems in Yemen (of which farmers paid a share), and a rehabilitation cost for pre-Columbian terraces (andenes) in Peru. A review also tabulates terracing costs from China of 1918 to 4045 USD per hectare (mechanisation, labour and socioeconomic costs), rising with the original slope from 5 to 25 degrees [ev_project_cost_wei16_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.conditionality: WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables for the documented technology, summed and converted to USD with the sheet's own exchange rate; they are not market prices, and older sheets treat every costed item as per hectare, so converted figures range from under a dollar to tens of thousands of USD per hectare; the sub-dollar sheets for Uganda and Niger and the Yemen sheet's figure look like entry or conversion problems rather than real costs. These are establishment costs, not costs per hectare restored, and the Peru, Jordan and Cabo Verde units come from upper-middle-income settings; the India costs are described by the evaluator as high by national norms and the Peru figure is a 1994 assessment cited secondhand. The Chinese terracing costs are a secondary table from an upper-middle-income setting and show that steeper land costs more to terrace [ev_project_cost_wei16_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the pooled per-hectare costs are a 1994 rehabilitation cost for Andean terraces in Peru from an FAO manual and Jordanian WOCAT sheets for a floodplain marab system costed over its ten hectares and mechanised Vallerani micro-catchment trenching costed per hectare [ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_5860_2021_establishment]. A review adds terracing costs from China of 1918 to 4045 USD per hectare, rising with the original slope from 5 to 25 degrees [ev_project_cost_wei16_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.conditionality: The Peruvian figure is a nominal 1994 cost for rehabilitating existing terraces rather than building new ones, and the Jordanian figures are the compilers' own cost tables converted at the sheets' stated rates, not market prices; all three sit outside the low- and lower-middle-income target band [ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_5860_2021_establishment]. The Chinese figures are a secondary table and include socioeconomic costs alongside machinery and labour [ev_project_cost_wei16_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.mechanism: Pooled units describe how siting and implementer affect what structures cost: in Karnataka, land-resource-inventory planning avoided unnecessary structures and lowered the construction cost of soil and water conservation works per hectare versus a conventional programme; in Ghana, the share of small dams rehabilitated below given per-irrigated-hectare cost thresholds differed between government and donor/NGO implementers. Field trials add on-farm savings: no-till with a residue mulch reduced total variable costs by 5% against conventional tillage in a Zimbabwe trial, and mulching reduced weed density and labour costs for weeding in an Ethiopian trial [ev_project_cost_mash25h1_5, ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.conditionality: Both are from lower-middle-income countries but measure different things: the India figure is an absolute construction cost per hectare from a lender completion report (the saving is relative to another SWC programme, not to no intervention), and the Ghana figure is a distribution of dam rehabilitation costs by implementer, not a cost reduction. What separates the sides: the reductions are each a comparison with an alternative on the same land (the Karnataka planning against a conventional programme, the trial plots against conventional tillage or no mulch), while the Ghana unit sits on the other side only as a spread of rehabilitation costs between implementers, with no comparison against doing otherwise. The Zimbabwe saving is for mulch bundled with no-till, and the Ethiopian saving is a weeding-labour statement without a figure [ev_project_cost_mash25h1_5, ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: In-field pits and bunds let more rain infiltrate and stay in the soil, so crops suffer less from dry spells: zaï gave 300–400 kg of sorghum per hectare in a low-rainfall year on degraded land where the without-zaï yield was 0, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years, and chololo pits in Tanzania are reported to conserve soil moisture and mitigate drought effects [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s, ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_7]. Stored water bridges dry spells: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss in critical drought periods, pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, and cisterns on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4]. Studies cited in conservation agriculture meta-analyses report yields 10–100% higher than conventional tillage in relatively dry years, a review notes soil and water conservation is particularly useful where rainfall is low or variable, and WOCAT compilers in Burkina Faso, Cambodia, Ethiopia, India, Somalia, Tunisia, Uzbekistan and other countries rate drought impacts as reduced, the Cambodian sheet noting the pond provides enough water even during drought [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_4, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_6, ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: The benefit fades as drought deepens: stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield gain in the driest year (1985), Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, zaï only reduces the impact of a dry spell of two to three weeks where soil water storage reaches 50 mm, and a water-harvesting review states that crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. Storage runs out: subsurface dams in Brazil tended to dry up in the rainless year 2001 and small dams cannot sustain long dry spells, and four consecutive drought years in Tunisia limited soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. In a semi-arid Kenyan season with a failed start, conservation agriculture pillars had no detectable effect on maize yields [ev_crop_yield_boil19_3]; in Ethiopia vegetation greenness in treated watersheds still tracked local drought severity [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4]. Much of the pool is WOCAT compiler ratings (the Haiti compiler says the impact is not yet measured), statements cited second-hand inside meta-analyses and reviews, an expert review, and bundled programmes in Rwanda and Ethiopia; the Brazilian cistern statement on livestock mortality in severe drought is a potential effect, not a measurement [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: In semi-arid fields, pits and bunds raise infiltration and soil water retention so crops suffer less from dry spells: zaï gave 300–400 kg of sorghum per hectare in a low-rainfall year on degraded land where the without-zaï yield was 0, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, and crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s, ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1]. In semi-arid Brazil, pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years, and production-cistern water is described as able to reduce animal mortality in more severe drought [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1]; subsurface dams in Brazil tended to dry up in the rainless year 2001 and small dams cannot sustain long dry spells [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]; and in a Kenyan season with a failed start and a long dry spell, conservation agriculture pillars had no detectable effect on maize yields, though the authors caution the yield data were aggregated [ev_crop_yield_boil19_3]. The positive units are field observations and secondary citations from West Africa, while the Brazilian statements are institutional assertions without data, the cistern statement framed as a potential effect [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: Pits and bunds let more rain infiltrate and stay in the soil, so crops suffer less from dry spells: zaï gave 300–400 kg of sorghum per hectare in a low-rainfall year on degraded land where the without-zaï yield was 0, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years, and chololo pits in Tanzania are reported to mitigate drought effects [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s, ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_7]. A water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, cisterns on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, Rwandan project households proved more resilient than controls to the 2016 drought, physical structures were reported to buffer crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia, and WOCAT compilers in Burkina Faso, Cambodia, Ethiopia, India, Somalia, Tunisia and Uzbekistan rate drought impacts as reduced [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: Stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield gain in the driest year (1985), Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, zaï only reduces the impact of a dry spell of two to three weeks where soil water storage reaches 50 mm, and a water-harvesting review states that crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. Four consecutive drought years in Tunisia limited soil-conservation benefits, conservation agriculture pillars had no detectable effect on maize in a Kenyan season with a failed start, reduced-tillage cotton in dry years in Mali and North Cameroon ranged from -10 to +20%, and in Ethiopia vegetation greenness in treated watersheds still tracked local drought severity [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1, ev_crop_yield_boil19_3, ev_crop_yield_roos10_1, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4]. Many units are WOCAT compiler ratings (the Haiti compiler says the impact is not yet measured) or secondary citations, and the Rwandan and Ethiopian results come from bundled programmes [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_drought_impacts].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: Rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss during critical drought periods, and in Mediterranean long-term experiments cited in a no-till meta-analysis, wheat yields under no-till tended to be higher than under conventional tillage in years when water stress occurred [ev_crop_yield_silv26_2, ev_crop_yield_pitt15_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: The same experiments show no-till wheat yields lower than conventional tillage in years with little water stress [ev_crop_yield_pitt15_5]. Both units are secondary citations inside a review and a meta-analysis drawn from several countries, with no magnitude, so they show direction only [ev_crop_yield_silv26_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: In semi-arid Brazil, pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in years of irregular rainfall, and production-cistern water is described as able to reduce animal mortality in more severe drought; a WOCAT compiler in Jordan rates drought impacts as reduced [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: Storage runs out in long droughts: subsurface dams in Brazil tended to dry up in the rainless year 2001, and small manually built dams cannot sustain long dry spells [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The positive units are institutional statements without data (the cistern statement framed as a potential effect) and a practitioner rating, while the failures come from field observation and family interviews [ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: In-field practices let more rain infiltrate and hold water in the soil, so crops suffer less from dry spells: zaï pits gave sorghum in a low-rainfall year on degraded land that otherwise yielded nothing, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, and crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. Conservation agriculture meta-analyses find immediate positive yield effects when water stress occurs during crop growth, because mulch improves the soil water balance, and maize yields under conservation agriculture generally above conventional practice in seasons with a precipitation balance below 200 mm, rising as conditions get drier [ev_crop_yield_corb20_8, ev_crop_yield_stew18_1]; in Malawi's El Niño drought season ground cover raised maize from 247 kg per hectare on control plots to 432 kg per hectare and raised the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement [ev_crop_yield_boil19_2, ev_food_security_boil19_1]. In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers obtained 1520 kg of maize per hectare against 368 kg on conventional plots in the 2006/07 season, which the source calls a drought year [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1]. In a Kenyan trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 2.53 against 1.82 t per hectare without inputs (not significant) and 4.10 against 3.15 t per hectare with manure and fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3]. Storage works carry water into dry periods: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, Indian farmers reported a 6% chance of crop failure from aberrant rains with a farm pond against 20% without, cisterns on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, and WOCAT compilers in Cambodia, Ethiopia, India, Tunisia, Somalia and other countries rate drought impacts as reduced [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. Sand dams carry water into drought years: in Zimbabwe the months water could be collected at sand-dam sites in a drought year rose from 5.8 before construction to 9.7 after, and in a Kenyan catchment with sand dams the number of people exposed to droughts fell from 420 to 0 while a control catchment stayed at 600 [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. Against the fertilised conventional arm in the same Zimbabwe budget the contrast was 1520 against 400 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_2]. In Zimbabwe's El Niño drought season, maize under no-till with a residue mulch yielded 31.8% more than under conventional tillage [ev_crop_yield_mash25h1_1]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, the plots without mulch were the ones particularly affected by the dry spells of the season [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm and 1-m half-moon plots mitigated the impact of dry spells by retaining moisture for 2-3 weeks [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. A Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. In Zambia, a review of conservation agriculture cites trial findings that higher soil moisture improved yields in poor seasons, showing the potential to reduce the risk of crop failure due to low or poorly distributed rainfall [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_3]. In on-farm conservation-farming trials in Kenya, Tanzania and Ethiopia the largest yield difference over conventional ploughing came in rainy seasons with low rainfall, when the practice maximises rainfall infiltration so the crop can bridge short periods of dry spell [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. In Zambia's 2001/2 season of very scattered rainfall, maize in hand-hoe conservation-farming basins yielded 3,054 kg per hectare against 1,339 kg under ploughing, which the authors say showcased the water-harvesting benefits of the basins [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1]. Farmers practising basins in Zambia, Zimbabwe and Limpopo reported maize and sorghum yields of >1 tonnes per hectare even in seasons with poor rainfall (<450 mm), against total crop failure under conventional ploughing [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_9]. In a Zimbabwe household panel, conservation agriculture (mostly planting basins, with residue mulch and rotation on some plots) improved maize yields during times of drought, and sorghum and cowpea yields too [ev_crop_yield_mich19_3, ev_crop_yield_mich19_5]. Crop-model (APSIM) runs on semi-arid Zimbabwe weather put the first-year maize difference between conservation agriculture and ploughing largely in seasons with below normal rainfall, and in the 1980/81 drought year 241 mm produced some maize grain under conservation agriculture and none under ploughing [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_1, ev_crop_yield_faocr11_3]. In Madagascar, rice sown without tillage on a dead mulch and rotated out-yielded tilled rice on hillside fields in three seasons that each had a month-long rainfall deficit [ev_crop_yield_brue14_6]. A commercial farmer in South Africa reported that his no-till, residue-cover and rotation system completely buffered his farm from mild droughts or dry spells through increased rainfall infiltration [ev_yield_stability_faocr11_10]. In Brazil, Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths, as easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: The benefit shrinks or vanishes in severe drought: stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield gain in the driest year (1985), Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, zaï only buffers a dry spell of two to three weeks where soil water storage is sufficient, and in Mozambique conservation agriculture and control plots alike failed completely in a drought season [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_1, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_2]. In the Kenyan trial's short rains with meteorological droughts, tied ridging gave no advantage (0.52 against 0.53 t per hectare without inputs, 1.17 against 1.27 with manure and fertiliser) because there was little or no rainwater to hold in the basins [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_4, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5, ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]. The pool now includes conservation agriculture meta-analyses and on-farm or trial measurements from Malawi, Kenya, Zimbabwe and Mozambique, but most units remain WOCAT compiler ratings or institutional assertions (the Haiti compiler says the impact is not yet measured); the Zimbabwe planting-basin gain also carries manure and fertiliser, the Indian pond figures come from a preprint farmer survey, the sand-dam figures rest on recall interviews, and the Rwandan and Ethiopian programme results come from bundled programmes [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_drought_impacts, ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4]. Not every in-field practice helped in that Malawi El Nino season: banking, the reinforcement of ridges while the crop is growing, cut maize from 245 to 153 kg per hectare and lowered the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement from 0.19 to 0.054 [ev_crop_yield_boil19_5, ev_food_security_boil19_3]. The Zimbabwe residue-mulch gain is one on-station season with no normal-year comparison, and the mulch is bundled with no-till [ev_crop_yield_mash25h1_1]. The Ethiopian dry-spell finding is a field observation of which plots wilted, not a tested yield contrast [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. The Burkina Faso half-moon and zaï moisture finding is the authors' statement about dry spells, for pits filled with compost [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. That Burkina Faso conclusion is the author's overall judgement, with no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. Water harvesting is not irrigation, and the new primaries mark the limit: at the more arid Kenyan sites of Laikipia and Machakos each site recorded complete crop failures in two out of three and four seasons, with 0 kg per hectare of maize harvested at Machakos due to meteorological drought, and the conservation-farming treatments did not avert it [ev_crop_yield_rock09_10]. The crop model shows the same limit: in seasons with 230 mm and 176 mm of in-crop rainfall there was total crop failure under both conservation agriculture and ploughing [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_2]. In Madagascar the severe drought of 2007–2008 could not be offset by the mulch-based system [ev_crop_yield_brue14_5], and in the Zimbabwe panel conservation agriculture had no specific impact in mitigating rainfall-shortfall losses for millet and groundnut [ev_crop_yield_mich19_6]. The East African low-rainfall gain is for the best system per site, ripping or pitting usually with fertiliser, so it is bundled with reduced tillage and fertiliser, and the authors read it as a trend from their own figure [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. The Zambia 2001/2 basin contrast is a raw comparison in a single season with no normal-year reference, and most basin farmers received hybrid seed, fertiliser and lime on credit, so part of the gap is the input package [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1]. The farmer-reported basin yields compare fertilised basins with unfertilised ploughing, which the author warns makes those datasets too confounded [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_9]. The Zimbabwe panel's drought-season gains are interaction estimates for conservation agriculture as practised (planting basins bundled with residue mulch and rotation); its normal-season results are reported in the production row, not here [ev_crop_yield_mich19_3, ev_crop_yield_mich19_5]. The semi-arid drought-year gains are simulations that bundle residue cover, better infiltration and fertiliser targeting, not measured seasons [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_1, ev_crop_yield_faocr11_3]. The Madagascar dry-spell gains bundle no-till, mulch and rotation and have no normal-year comparison [ev_crop_yield_brue14_6]. The South African statement is a single commercial farmer's before-and-after testimony for a residue-cover system with no capture structure [ev_yield_stability_faocr11_10]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. The Zambia review statement is cited secondhand, gives no magnitude and has no normal-year comparison, and the trial behind it bundles reduced tillage with residue retention [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: Two sub-practices carry this cell and they work differently. In-field practices let more rain infiltrate and hold water in the soil, so crops suffer less from dry spells: zaï pits gave sorghum in a low-rainfall year on degraded land that otherwise yielded nothing, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, and crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. Storage practices — ponds, cisterns, sand and subsurface dams — work instead through water kept for later use: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells, Indian farmers reported a 6% chance of crop failure from aberrant rains with a farm pond against 20% without, production-cistern water for livestock can reduce animal deaths in severe drought and pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in semi-arid Brazil, cisterns on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, and in Zimbabwe the months water could be collected at sand-dam sites in a drought year rose from 5.8 before construction to 9.7 after [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1]. Against the fertilised conventional arm in the same Zimbabwe budget the contrast was 1520 against 400 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_2]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, the plots without mulch were the ones particularly affected by the dry spells of the season [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. The two carry almost equal weight and the vote lands on low.
