water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: Small storage works fail in prolonged drought: subsurface dams at Mutuca (Pesqueira) tended to dry up through 2001, a year without rain, and those at Ouricuri do not withstand long droughts because of their small size; this records a shortfall in benefit rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The benefit side rests on a compiler rating and on institutional statements with no data in the passage (an Embrapa assessment of technologies it promotes and a cistern statement of potential), while the dry-up evidence is field observation and family interviews; the pool covers only Brazil and Jordan [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8].

water_harvesting_conservation__establish.mechanism: Pooled costs are up-front construction costs per structure: village ponds or tanks and dry-stone check dams (the latter per cubic metre of masonry) from a World Bank watershed project in Himachal Pradesh, India, and compiler-reported WOCAT establishment costs for a farm pond with irrigation system in Cambodia, a set of check dams and walls in India, a 200 m vetiver line in Haiti, a fascine line in Madagascar and a haffir in Somalia.
water_harvesting_conservation__establish.conditionality: The WOCAT figures are each compiler's own cost table summed and converted with the sheet's exchange rate, and the India project figures are self-reported from project monitoring in rupees converted at one rate; none are market prices. A structure means very different things across the pool, from a fascine line of a few metres to a haffir of about 5100 square metres, and the per-cubic-metre check-dam figure is per volume of masonry, so the pooled cost class is a loose summary rather than a comparable unit cost.

water_harvesting_conservation__fire__all.mechanism: The practices limit fire mainly by removing fuel: on intensively tended terraces all crop residues are grazed off as soon as harvests end, so bush fires have little to spread on, and the Vallerani compiler in Burkina Faso keeps the treated area open to regulated grazing to cut the grass growth that could carry a fire, with herders also watching the area [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_fire_risk]. WOCAT compilers for bench terraces in Bangladesh and stone check walls and check dams in India also rate fire risk as reduced [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_4284_2018_fire_risk, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_fire_risk].
water_harvesting_conservation__fire__all.conditionality: The terrace statement is an expert estimate that its authors say has no experimental basis on terraces, and the other units are WOCAT practitioner ratings, the Bangladesh and India ones without any stated reasoning [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1]. The effect depends on grazing or other management keeping biomass down rather than on the structures themselves.

water_harvesting_conservation__flood__al.mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and infiltration trenches slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces lowered mean runoff and flood peaks on small mountain plots, stone bunds lower peak discharges at the foot of the slope, trenches significantly reduced plot runoff across the reviewed studies, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment reduced flood runoff volume, clipped peaks and lengthened flood duration [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s]. A check-dam review cites check dams mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow in Iran and check-dam sequences proving effective against strong floods in Italian torrents, and small hill dams in Morocco are credited with damping damage during the serious 2002-2003 floods [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. Spate and diversion structures in Yemen are reported to control floods, users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive flood limitation as a benefit, compacted hill terraces in Uttarakhand, India are credited with limiting flood and landslide damage, and WOCAT compilers across sheets from Ethiopia, Kenya, Tunisia, Somalia, Uzbekistan and other countries rate flooding as reduced, the Kenyan compiler noting a dam or series of dams buffers downstream flooding [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding]. Embrapa credits its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in Brazil, with easing floods as well [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__flood__al.conditionality: The same check-dam review finds a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where structures were ill-designed and not maintained [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3]. Diversion structures can work the other way: diversion banquettes in Niger raised peak discharges, runoff-diversion systems accelerate concentration time, and larger sand dams increase flooding risk [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3, ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1]. Catchment-level terrace evidence is scarce, most measured results are at plot or hillslope scale, the Tunisian catchment result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, and the Italian check-dam cases are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting rather than farm water harvesting [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2]. Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings: the Philippine sheet rates flood impacts as worse, the Indian farm-pond sheet rates downstream flooding as unchanged, the Zambian compiler says the benefit holds only at large scale, and a Somali sheet scores downstream flooding in the worsening direction although its comment says flooding was reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_flooding]. The barraginha flood statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, unmeasured, and a landscape-scale effect rather than one on the adopting farm [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__flood__al.mechanism: Bunds, terraces and small dams hold or slow runoff: stone bunds lower peak discharges at the foot of the slope and protect land from rapid flow in heavy rain, a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment cut the runoff volume of 71 single-peak floods by 50 percent and clipped peaks, compacted hill terraces in Uttarakhand, India are credited with mitigating massive floods and landslides, and small hill dams in Morocco are credited with damping damage during the serious 2002-2003 floods [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_2, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. Spate and diversion structures in Yemen are reported to control floods, small-reservoir users in Ghana list flood limitation as a benefit, and WOCAT compilers from Ethiopia, Kenya, Niger, Rwanda, Somalia, Tunisia, Uzbekistan and other countries rate flooding as reduced, noting that dams create a buffer, that stone lines and walls reduce peak flows during heavy rainfall and that more water is trapped in the catchment [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1553_2012_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts].

water_harvesting_conservation__flood__al.conditionality: The Philippine sheet for conservation tillage in corn rates flood impacts in the worsening direction [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_flood_impacts]. water_harvesting_conservation__flood__mi.conditionality: This row keeps only evidence from low- and lower-middle-income settings, so the check-dam review cases behind the wider flood row (peak-flow reductions and torrent control from higher-income settings), the plot-scale terrace and trench measurements and the Brazilian barraginha statement drop out, and nothing here is measured at severe or extreme floods. Diversion structures can work the other way: diversion banquettes in Niger raised peak discharges [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1]. Catchment-level evidence is scarce, and the Tunisian catchment result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s]. Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings rather than measurements: the Indian farm-pond sheet rates downstream flooding as unchanged, the Zambian compiler says the benefit holds only at large scale, and a Somali sheet scores downstream flooding in the worsening direction although its comment says flooding was reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_flooding]. water_harvesting_conservation__flood_haz.mechanism: Terraces, contour stone bunds and lines, check dams, sand dams and water-spreading structures slow and spread runoff and retain water and sediment, lowering peak discharges and lengthening flood rise times; in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment a combined treatment cut the runoff volume of 71 single-peak floods by 50%, and WOCAT compilers for many of these structures judge downstream flooding reduced. Users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive fewer rainy-season floods, and spate and diversion structures in Yemen are said to control floods. A check-dam review cites check dams mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow in Iran and check-dam sequences proving effective against strong floods in Italian torrents, and small hill dams in Morocco are credited with damping damage in the serious 2002-2003 floods [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. Embrapa credits its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in Brazil, with easing floods as well [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__flood_haz.conditionality: Most units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, and catchment-scale measurement is scarce, with a review calling the terrace effect on peak flow uncertain; the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, and the Yemen and Uttarakhand statements are lender self-reported. Direction depends on design: diversion banquettes in Niger and runoff-diversion dikes raised peak flows, larger sand dams increase flooding risk, a conservation-tillage sheet from the Philippines rated flood impacts worse, and a farm pond in India was rated neutral. The same review finds check dams have a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where ill-designed or poorly maintained; its positive cases are secondary citations, and the Italian ones are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2]. The barraginha flood statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, unmeasured, and a landscape-scale effect rather than one on the adopting farm [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.mechanism: A maize meta-regression finds conservation agriculture performs better relative to conventional practice under drought and/or heat stress, and a review of quasi-experimental studies reports that the impact of soil and water conservation is especially significant in areas with temperature shocks or lower rainfall [ev_crop_yield_stew18_2, ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.conditionality: Neither unit separates heat from drought: the meta-regression frames them together and the review groups temperature shocks with low rainfall, without naming specific practices or giving a magnitude, so no unit isolates heat-stress losses [ev_crop_yield_stew18_2, ev_crop_yield_mala24_5]. The meta-regression is restricted to maize under conservation agriculture, so it speaks to in-field residue and tillage practices rather than to storage structures [ev_crop_yield_stew18_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.mechanism: A maize meta-regression finds conservation agriculture performs better relative to conventional practice under drought and/or heat stress, and a review of quasi-experimental studies reports that the impact of soil and water conservation is especially significant in areas with temperature shocks or lower rainfall [ev_crop_yield_stew18_2, ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.conditionality: Neither unit separates heat from drought: the meta-regression frames them together and the review groups temperature shocks with low rainfall, without naming specific practices or giving a magnitude, so no unit isolates heat-stress losses [ev_crop_yield_stew18_2, ev_crop_yield_mala24_5]. The meta-regression is restricted to maize under conservation agriculture, so it speaks to in-field residue and tillage practices rather than to storage structures [ev_crop_yield_stew18_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: Water harvesting and conservation structures capture runoff and raise soil moisture so rainfed crops yield more, especially in dry years and low-rainfall areas; stored water allows supplemental irrigation and extra crops, and sediment and organic matter trapped behind structures add fertility. Meta-analyses now carry much of the evidence: A meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds a pooled yield gain of 71% over controls, with 142% for infiltration pits, 91% for mulching, 69% for soil and stone bunds, 48% for terraces and 74% for tied ridging [ev_crop_yield_tefe24_1, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_2, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_3, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_4, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_5, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_6]; a synthesis of Ethiopian studies gives mean grain-yield differences of 322 kg per hectare for stone bunds, 554.3 for tied ridges and 629.2 for mulching [ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_4]; a sub-Saharan conservation agriculture meta-analysis finds yields 3.7% above conventional tillage overall, 8.4% for maize when all three principles are applied and 12.5% at sites with under 400 mm of seasonal rainfall, with the gain growing slowly over time [ev_crop_yield_corb20_1, ev_crop_yield_corb20_4, ev_crop_yield_corb20_6, ev_crop_yield_corb20_10]; and a terracing meta-analysis finds biomass on terraces about 1.94 times that on slopes, and reviewed studies report terraced teff, barley and maize yields at least two times those on slopes and 20% gains on young bench terraces in Peru [ev_crop_yield_wei16_1, ev_crop_yield_wei16_2, ev_crop_yield_wei16_4]. In Burkina Faso stone bunds raised sorghum yields by 33% to 55% and by about 142% with compost, on-farm trials in Mozambique gave maize gains of 504 to 800 kg per hectare on planting basins and direct-seeded plots, in Malawi's El Niño season ground cover raised maize from 247 to 432 kg per hectare, and silt farmland behind check dams on China's Loess Plateau yields 6–10 times more than sloping farmland [ev_crop_yield_zoug14_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_3, ev_crop_yield_boil19_2, ev_crop_yield_luca21_1]. Stored water stabilises output: Indian farmers reported crop-failure chances falling from 20% to 6% in the rainy season and from 100% to 5–10% in winter with a farm pond, sand dams cut crop failure against a control catchment in Kenya, and WOCAT compilers across many technology sheets judge crop, fodder and animal production increased [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_yield_stability_pals23_2, ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1]. In a Zimbabwe enterprise budget first-year planting-basin conservation farming yielded 1520 kg of maize per hectare against 400 kg on the fertilised conventional arm [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_2]. Newer field trials point the same way: In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, maize stalk mulch raised maize yield over no mulch at both sites in both seasons, and planting basins did so in 2012 [ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_1, ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_2, ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_3, ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_4, ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_6, ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_8]. In Rwanda, vetiver mulch raised maize to 8089 kg per hectare against 4755 on flat rainfed plots [ev_crop_yield_uwiz18h1_1], and in the same trial runoff from the terrace waterways, collected in a dug, lined pond and applied by a gravity drip kit as supplementary irrigation, gave 11982 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_uwiz18h1_3]. In Burkina Faso, crop yields in years of average rainfall rose by 63–74 per cent on farms using rock bunds and by over 100 per cent on farms using zaï [ev_crop_yield_sawa11h1_1, ev_crop_yield_sawa11h1_2]. On crusted degraded soil in Burkina Faso, 30-cm zaï and 1-m half-moons with compost gave 408 and 1372 kg of millet per hectare where direct seeding gave none [ev_crop_yield_zour25h1_1, ev_crop_yield_zour25h1_2]. In Zimbabwe's El Niño drought season, maize under no-till with a residue mulch yielded 31.8% more than under conventional tillage [ev_crop_yield_mash25h1_1]. A review cites soil and water conservation structures combined with biological measures raising wheat production by 30–45% over business-as-usual [ev_crop_yield_tade23h1_2]. Soils on Burkina Faso farms using soil and water conservation techniques had higher nitrogen contents than the control farm, used here as a component [ev_soil_nitrogen_sawa11h1_4]. Primary trials and surveys from eastern and southern Africa now stand in for second-hand Zambia readings. In on-farm trials in Ethiopia, ripper plus tied ridging with fertiliser gave 1775 kg of maize per hectare against 1458 under conventional maresha ploughing with the same fertiliser, and 1076 against 945 kg of tef [ev_crop_yield_rock09_1, ev_crop_yield_rock09_4]; in Tanzania, ripping and pitting combined with fertilisation gave yields 1.5–2.2 times those of conventional ploughing with the same fertilisation [ev_crop_yield_rock09_11]; and at Chipata, Zambia, basins with fertiliser gave 6660 kg of maize per hectare against 3153 under conventional practice [ev_crop_yield_rock09_13]. In Zambia's 2001/2 season hand-hoe conservation-farming basins gave 3,054 kg of maize per hectare against 1,339 under ploughing, and a regression controlling for planting date, hybrid seed and fertiliser puts the gain from the basins themselves closer to 700 kg per hectare for maize and 400 to 500 kg for cotton [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1, ev_crop_yield_hagg03_2, ev_crop_yield_hagg03_3]; a later survey of Zambian conservation-agriculture households reports 5.2 t of maize per hectare in basins against 1.8 under the hand hoe [ev_crop_yield_umar11_1]. A meta-analysis of tied-ridge-furrow experiments finds tied ridges without fertiliser or mulch yielded 17% more sorghum grain than flat planting [ev_crop_yield_makm21_1]. In Madagascar, rice sown without tillage on a dead mulch and rotated averaged 2.8 against 2.6 t per hectare on lowland and 2.4 against 2.1 on hillside fields, and year-to-year variability fell after consecutive years under the system (a 6% and a 13% decrease in the coefficient of variation) [ev_crop_yield_brue14_1, ev_crop_yield_brue14_2, ev_yield_stability_brue14_3, ev_yield_stability_brue14_4]. Crop-model (APSIM) runs on semi-arid Zimbabwe weather give higher maize yields under conservation agriculture than under ploughing when aggregated across seasons, and more stable yields across different types of seasons [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_5, ev_yield_stability_faocr11_6]. In a Zimbabwe household panel, conservation agriculture (mostly planting basins, with residue mulch and rotation on some plots) improved maize yields both when rainfall was above average and during times of drought, and sorghum and cowpea yields during drought [ev_crop_yield_mich19_3, ev_crop_yield_mich19_4, ev_crop_yield_mich19_5]. A review of conservation agriculture in Zambia also cites planting basins plus lime raising yields by 68% [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_1], a simulated gain of around 40% for the whole conservation farming package [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_6], higher soil moisture improving yields in poor seasons [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_3], and global syntheses: reduced tillage and crop residue management associated with a 106% increase in cereal yields, an average yield improvement of over 100% for smallholder conservation agriculture across 286 developing-country case studies, and a slight increase over conventional tillage, growing over time and especially in dry conditions, across 25 long-term trials [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_13, ev_crop_yield_arsl15_15, ev_crop_yield_arsl15_16].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Held out of the class, as a caveat on where the practice performs rather than as production evidence: where rainfall is heavy the practice can lower yields through waterlogging, and the authors say so. Annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected the performance of Ethiopian soil and water conservation practices negatively, which the synthesis puts down to water logging on the furrows of structures, and fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_adim16_6, ev_crop_yield_adim16_2]; plots with bunds yielded less than non-conserved plots in high-rainfall western Amhara [ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_10]; in the Sudanian zone of Cameroon, where rain exceeds 80 mm a day and 1,200 mm a year, sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than flat-cultivated fields because of frequent waterlogging and the risk of nutrient leaching [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]; 92% of the data in a conservation agriculture review show mulch cover in high-rainfall areas lowering yields through waterlogging [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3]; and at sites with over 1,200 mm of seasonal rainfall conservation agriculture yielded 4.3% less than conventional tillage [ev_crop_yield_corb20_7]. In a wetter sub-humid Kenyan site, ridged plots with fertiliser gave the lowest yields, slightly below conventional practice, which the authors say can probably be explained by waterlogging caused by ridging [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6]. Read these as a siting limit: the practice should not be applied where rainfall is that heavy. Other measured losses do count against the class: bunds cut yields by up to 7% in the first few years in Ethiopia, and stone bunds in semi-arid Tanzania reduced maize yield by 13% [ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adim16_9]. The sub-Saharan conservation agriculture meta-analysis finds no significant gain for crops other than maize, and outperformance of conventional tillage only with no-tillage systems rather than planting basins or minimum tillage [ev_crop_yield_corb20_3, ev_crop_yield_corb20_9]; a maize meta-regression finds conservation agriculture consistently underperforms on high-clay soils in very wet seasons, though at median rainfall and clay it outperforms conventional practice even without fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_stew18_3, ev_crop_yield_stew18_4]; and in drought seasons in Mozambique and Zimbabwe conservation agriculture gave no harvest or yielded less than conventional tillage [ev_crop_yield_thierf15_1, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_7]. In Algeria farmers lost 5 to 15% of their cropped area to banquettes without seeing yields improve, legume yields between banquettes showed no significant gain, and a Moroccan farmer saw no yield improvement between banquettes imposed by technicians [ev_crop_yield_arab04_1, ev_crop_yield_arab04_2, ev_crop_yield_roos10_2]. Other nulls and negatives: conservation promoted mostly off-farm had no yield effect, benefits in Ethiopia appeared only once structures were maintained for at least seven years, diversion banquettes in Niger cut yields, and soil salinisation can appear on check-dam farmland [ev_crop_yield_luca21_1]. Outside the meta-analyses the pool mixes independent evaluations with lender completion-report figures, bundled watershed programmes, reviews quoting ranges from earlier studies, a farmer survey reported in a preprint and many practitioner judgements; much of the zai and planting-basin gain rides on added manure, compost or fertiliser [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1]. In the Malawi El Nino survey banking, the reinforcement of ridges while the crop is growing, cut maize from 245 to 153 kg per hectare, so some in-field practices lowered yield in that season [ev_crop_yield_boil19_5]. Planting basins gave no significant gain over no mulch in 2011 at either Ethiopian site (4239 against 4171 and 4265 against 4131 kg per hectare) [ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_5, ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_7]. Rwandan contour ridges were not significantly different from flat rainfed plots (5937 against 4755 kg per hectare) [ev_crop_yield_uwiz18h1_2]. The Burkina Faso zaï and half-moon contrasts are against land where direct seeding produced no grain, with compost added to the pits, so they measure bringing degraded land into production rather than an improvement on a cropped field. The Burkina Faso farm gains are for years the authors call average rainfall, with compost on the bunded fields. The Zimbabwe residue-mulch gain is one on-station season with no normal-year comparison, and the mulch is bundled with no-till [ev_crop_yield_mash25h1_1]. The wheat figure is a review's citation of a package that includes biological measures [ev_crop_yield_tade23h1_2]. The Rwandan pond result is a bundle — terrace runoff capture, a lined storage pond and drip irrigation — so the yield is delivered through irrigation hardware and cannot be read as a pure capture effect; it is one season of a randomised trial in which every plot received farmyard manure and mineral fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_uwiz18h1_3]. The East African and Zambian trial gains are bundles. In Ethiopia the comparator carried the same fertiliser, but without fertiliser neither improved tillage nor fertiliser alone raised maize significantly, and the 20–50% tef gain without fertiliser was not significant [ev_crop_yield_rock09_2, ev_crop_yield_rock09_3]; the Tanzanian ripping-or-pitting arms are bundled with reduced tillage [ev_crop_yield_rock09_11]; and the Chipata basins carried improved seed against a conventional practice with extremely low fertiliser, in seasons of well-above-average rainfall, a gain the authors say cannot be fully explained [ev_crop_yield_rock09_13]. Some trial arms lost: pitting with fertiliser was the lowest-yielding treatment at Machakos, at 1.2 against 1.6 t per hectare under conventional practice [ev_crop_yield_rock09_9], and at the more arid Kenyan sites each site recorded complete crop failures in two out of three and four seasons, which the treatments did not avert; water harvesting is not irrigation [ev_crop_yield_rock09_10]. The Zambian 2001/2 raw contrast is one season with no normal-year reference and mixes the basin effect with higher input use, since most basin farmers received hybrid seed, fertiliser and lime on credit; the regression figure is the cleaner estimate, and even its basin dummy also picks up extra weeding labour and lime [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1, ev_crop_yield_hagg03_2]. The later Zambian survey yields are farmer self-reports with large spreads, and the basin gain over ploughing (5.2 against 3.8 t per hectare) was not significant [ev_crop_yield_umar11_1, ev_crop_yield_umar11_2]; a national Zambian smallholder panel finds no significant maize yield effect of planting basins under any of its estimators [ev_crop_yield_burk12_1]; and paired soil samples on Zambian fields under basins or ripping (bundled with reduced tillage), with residues hardly retained, showed no significant difference in nitrogen [ev_soil_nitrogen_umar11_6]. The Zimbabwe panel keeps drought-season and normal-season results apart: in average rainfall periods conservation agriculture had no significant impact on any crop, in another specification it decreased maize yields by itself, and it did not mitigate rainfall-shortfall or surplus losses for millet and groundnut, so its gains appear only in seasons away from the average [ev_crop_yield_mich19_1, ev_crop_yield_mich19_2, ev_crop_yield_mich19_6, ev_crop_yield_mich19_7]. The tied-ridge meta-analysis finds no significant millet gain over flat planting and no significant difference when grass mulch was added to the ridges, and its sorghum observation count is internally inconsistent [ev_crop_yield_makm21_3, ev_crop_yield_makm21_2, ev_crop_yield_makm21_1]. In Madagascar the severe drought of 2007–2008 could not be offset by the system, and the pooled comparison showed no change in yield variance, the stability gain appearing only after consecutive years; the rice gains bundle no-till, mulch and rotation [ev_crop_yield_brue14_5, ev_yield_stability_brue14_7]. The crop-model results are simulations that bundle residue cover, better infiltration and fertiliser targeting; under sub-humid weather the model gives no difference [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_4], and in seasons with 230 mm and 176 mm of in-crop rainfall there was total crop failure under both systems [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_2]. Farmer reports of basin yields of >1 tonnes per hectare in poor-rainfall seasons, against total failure under ploughing, compare fertilised basins with unfertilised ploughing, which the author calls too confounded [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_9]. The remaining Zambia and global figures are cited secondhand in Arslan and colleagues' literature review, and none has a normal-year comparison: the 68% gain is for planting basins plus lime application, with timely conventional farming giving 50% in the same trials [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_1]; the roughly 40% gain is a simulation of the whole conservation farming package, through early planting and improved soil quality [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_6]; the 106% is for reduced tillage together with residue management [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_13]; the poor-season result bundles reduced tillage with residue retention [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_3]; the over-100% figure comes from purposely selected best-practice projects [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_15]; and the long-term trials are mainly from North America, Australia and Europe [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_16]. Readings in that review that misread their primaries were dropped, and the primaries themselves are now in the pool directly.

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In the tropical highlands, soil and water conservation has measured yield gains and measured yield losses, depending on the practice. Gains: an Ethiopian synthesis finds mean grain-yield gains of 322 kg per hectare for stone bunds, 554.3 for tied ridges and 629.2 for mulching, stone and soil bunds raising yields by up to 10% in Tigray, and stone bunds raising soil total nitrogen from 0.16 to 0.20% [ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_4, ev_crop_yield_adim16_8, ev_soil_nitrogen_adim16_1]; in a Kenyan highland trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 4.10 against 3.15 t of maize per hectare with manure and fertiliser, and 2.53 against 1.82 t without inputs (not significant), and tended to give less variable yields [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_yield_stability_ndun23_1]; in Peru, 2 to 4-year old bench terraces gave 20% greater yields than adjacent sloping fields [ev_crop_yield_wei16_4]. Losses: in the same Ethiopian synthesis fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare, bunds cut yields by up to 7% in the first few years, and annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively, which the authors suggest may be waterlogging in the furrows of structures [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: The class is set by the gains. The fanya juu and soil bund losses and the finding that annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively are held out of it, because the synthesis puts that effect down to excessive water availability (water logging) on the furrows of structures [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]: they are logged as a performance caveat — these structures should not be applied where rainfall is that heavy — rather than as production evidence. The evidence points to three things that separate gains from losses. Practice type: stone bunds, tied ridges and mulching gained, while graded and level fanya juu, soil bunds and grass strips lost yield in the Ethiopian table [ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_2]. Rainfall: the gaining practices were studied at lower average rainfall (695.1 mm for tied ridges, 876.7 mm for mulching) than the losing bunds (1030.2 to 1454.3 mm), and rainfall above 1000 mm reduced performance [ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]; practice and rainfall travel together in that table, so the two cannot be fully separated. Time: bunds lose yield in the first few years [ev_crop_yield_adim16_7]. For a Task Team Leader the actionable reading is to match the structure to the rainfall regime, favouring in-field moisture capture in drier highlands and avoiding fanya juu and soil bunds where waterlogging is likely, and to budget for an early yield dip. At the dry end, tied ridging gave no advantage in the Kenyan short rains with meteorological droughts, since there was little rain to hold [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_4, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5]. On quality, both sides rest mainly on the same Ethiopian synthesis of unweighted means pooled across studies; the Kenyan result is a single-site trial whose lower-variability finding was not tested, and the Peruvian figure is cited in a review [ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_yield_stability_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_wei16_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In semi-arid settings, pits (zai, tassa), stone bunds, tied furrows and subsurface dams concentrate scarce rainfall in the root zone or store it for later use, raising cereal yields and enabling harvests in drought years when untreated fields fail.
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Evidence mixes Sahelian field results (Burkina Faso, Niger) with Embrapa and cistern-programme sources from semi-arid Brazil, several of them self-assessments or expert statements; the Brazilian programme effects are on value of production, a proxy, and some yield gains depend on manure added to the pits.

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In rainfed hill and watershed systems, in-situ rainwater conservation, terracing and soil and water conservation works combined with crop packages raise yields: average rainfed crop yields rose 24% and 26% against controls in Karnataka watershed phases, rainfed crop productivity rose 20.8 percent by difference-in-difference in Uttarakhand, and maize on terraced Rwandan hillsides rose from 1.5 to 2.8 tons per hectare [ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1, ev_crop_yield_utk22_1, ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7]. The DIME evaluation reported for Rwanda found the value of harvests 36 percent higher than in the control group [ev_agricultural_production_value_rwa18_3]. Outside these programmes, on-farm trials in Mozambique gave maize gains of 504 to 800 kg per hectare on planting basins and direct-seeded conservation agriculture over conventional ridge-and-furrow plots, and farmers in a Kenyan sand-dam catchment had less crop failure than in a control catchment [ev_crop_yield_thierf15_3, ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: The Indian and Rwandan units are bundled programmes in which conservation works came with improved seed, vermicompost, crop packages or life-saving irrigation, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated, and they are drawn from Bank completion reports or IEG reviews of them; the Rwanda maize figure is project monitoring without a control and the Uttarakhand terrace figure compares with- and without-project models [ev_crop_yield_hp17_2, ev_crop_yield_utk22_8, ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1, ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7]. In Mozambique conservation agriculture and control plots alike gave no maize or cowpea harvest in a drought season, and the Kenyan crop-failure finding comes from interviews [ev_crop_yield_thierf15_1, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_2, ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: Sand dams in Zimbabwe improved water availability, and livestock health improved at eight sites where cattle had been driven up to 20 km to the nearest water point before construction [ev_livestock_productivity_lazurko24_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Against this, long-term Zimbabwe trials found conventional tillage yielding considerably more maize than mulched and reduced-tillage treatments in extreme seasons, with no water-conservation benefit from mulch in the 1991/1992 drought [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_7]. The livestock finding rests on respondent statements, and both findings come from Zimbabwe only.

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In the Brazilian semi-arid, subsurface dams, tied furrows, micro-catchments with rescue irrigation and production cisterns store or concentrate water, raising crop productivity, enabling extra harvests and expanding the value of family production; in the Andes, infiltration trenches raised yields on some plots.
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Upper-middle-income evidence only, largely Embrapa and programme self-assessments plus one quasi-experimental study of value of production (a proxy); a trench review from Peru reports both positive and negative yield effects, and one cistern-programme author states there are no quantitative impact evaluations.

water_harvesting_conservation__recurrent.mechanism: Pooled costs are compiler-reported annual maintenance costs from WOCAT technology sheets, per hectare for sheets in Tunisia, India, Ethiopia, Yemen, Uganda, Jordan and Somalia and per structure for a farm pond in Cambodia, check dams in India, a vetiver line in Haiti, a fascine line in Madagascar and a haffir in Somalia; the cost class is set from the per-hectare sheets.
water_harvesting_conservation__recurrent.conditionality: WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables for the documented technology, summed and converted to USD with the sheet's own exchange rate; they are not market prices. Older sheets treat every costed item as per hectare, and the per-hectare values run from a cent to several hundred USD per hectare per year, so the sub-dollar Uganda and India figures look like entry or conversion problems; the Jordan sheet is an upper-middle-income case.

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: Higher and more stable yields, irrigation of gardens and higher-value crops from stored water, and better fodder and livestock raise household income and food security; beneficiaries shift from staples to vegetables, and a quasi-experimental study cited in a review found soil and water conservation raised net rice profit in Ghana by a significant 16 per cent [ev_household_income_veno12_2, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_economic_return_mala24_1]. WOCAT compilers describe the same pathway: planting pits in Uganda keep banana stands fruiting through drought and raise harvests for sale, ripper tillage in Zambia gives better tolerance to dry spells at lower tillage cost, farm ponds in Cambodia supply irrigation during drought, and contour stone bunds in Bhutan enlarge the cultivable area for diverse crops [ev_food_security_wocat_1587_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1587_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1139_2013_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1139_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_risk_of_production_failure]. WOCAT compilers' own benefit-versus-cost ratings point the same way, judging the long-term returns on both establishment and maintenance positive or very positive on nearly every sheet. In Kenya, farmers living near sand dams saw average income rise by 60% as more water in dry periods raised farm yields [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. An Ethiopian synthesis reports positive net present values of 3486.2 Birr per hectare for stone bunds, 2794.0 for bench terraces and 5283.4 for level fanya juu [ev_economic_return_adim16_1, ev_economic_return_adim16_2, ev_economic_return_adim16_3]; In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers earned a maize gross margin of 473.36 USD per hectare against 70.60 on conventional plots in the low-rainfall budget, with 866.84 against 357.16 for experienced farmers in high rainfall [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2]; and ground cover raised the odds of a Malawian plot meeting the household maize requirement in the El Niño season, and planting basins sharply raised those odds in a good Kenyan season [ev_food_security_boil19_1, ev_food_security_boil19_2]. Reviews add that rainwater-harvesting ponds brought statistically significant gains in household income and food security in Burkina Faso, water storage gave Ethiopian smallholders greater income security, harvested water used with precision irrigation in Ethiopia reached a net water value of up to 1.53 USD per cubic metre, and benefit-cost ratios of up to 3.38 with payback periods of 6.8 to 12 years; Indian farms with a farm pond reported net returns of 857 USD per hectare against 586 without [ev_household_income_silv26_1, ev_household_income_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_silv26_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. Modelled bench-terrace gains in Peru could raise per capita incomes by up to 15%, and a review tabulates significantly increased food security and incomes from check dams and infiltration pits in Malawi [ev_household_income_wei16_1, ev_food_security_ngur26_1]. Against the fertilised conventional arm in the same Zimbabwe budget the first-year margin was 473.36 against 48.19 US dollars per hectare [ev_economic_return_mazv09_3]. In Zimbabwe's El Niño season, no-till with a residue mulch returned a cost-benefit ratio of 1.39 against 1.05 for conventional tillage [ev_economic_return_mash25h1_3]. A review cites reduced tillage with residue maintained giving the highest net benefit and marginal rate of return on teff [ev_economic_return_tade23h1_4]. On crusted degraded soil in Burkina Faso, 1-m half-moons with compost were profitable at 377 275 FCFA per hectare after the investment [ev_economic_return_zour25h1_3]. Higher yields are cited as improving household food security in Burkina Faso, especially on farms that apply manure or some kind of soil and water conservation on over half their plots [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5]. A review cites soil and water conservation measures, including level bunds and fanya juu terraces, boosting farmer income by increasing soil fertility, yield and water [ev_household_income_tade23h1_1]. In Zambia, crop budgets for hand-hoe conservation-farming basins give returns per hectare 70 percent higher than conventional hand hoe cultivation and 150 percent higher than conventional plowing for cotton, and returns to land and to peak-season labor 60 to 90 percent higher than hand hoe tillage for maize [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_hagg03_7, ev_economic_return_hagg03_8]. In Brazil, an Embrapa survey of some communities found small-farm incomes rose by about half a minimum wage per month after the second filling of the barraginhas, and adopters rated food security as the technology's largest impact [ev_household_income_mira19_1, ev_food_security_mira19_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: The roll-up states conflicting evidence because the sub-practice rows disagree: the runoff-catchment, micro-catchment, spate and terracing rows each lean positive, while the in-field and cross-family rows are each split between gains and losses. What pulls the in-field side apart is how the gain is valued and against what. Crop budgets built on bundled input packages, and the practitioner ratings, put basins well ahead [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_hagg03_8, ev_economic_return_mazv09_1]; but a Zimbabwe household panel that values predicted yields with inputs held constant finds conservation agriculture (mostly planting basins, with residue mulch and rotation on some plots) generates less revenue than traditional cultivation over a large portion of the rainfall distribution, and its revenue comes out ahead only when rainfall is far from the mean [ev_economic_return_mich19_8]. The other losses are season- or practice-specific: banking in Malawi's El Nino season, tied ridging in a Kenyan drought season, and 30-cm zaï on a Burkina Faso trial [ev_food_security_boil19_3, ev_economic_return_ndun23_1, ev_economic_return_zour25h1_4]. In the cross-family row, gains from bundled programmes and cistern income sit against costs exceeding gains: single soil and water conservation measures not covering their annual costs in Burkina Faso, negative net present values for graded Ethiopian structures, a Brazilian production-cistern benefit-cost ratio far below break-even, and Niger families with soil and water conservation still in deficit in low-rainfall years [ev_economic_return_zoug14_3, ev_economic_return_adim16_4, ev_economic_return_casag22_9, ev_food_security_kabo04_1]; there farm size, how household labour is costed, where structures are built and the rainfall year separate the sides. Most pooled units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT technology sheets, including compilers' benefit-versus-cost judgements rather than measured returns, and much of the literature comes from bundled watershed programmes and lender completion or appraisal reports, so measured household effects are a minority. Independent evaluations are more cautious: no significant effect on food security or total income in Ethiopian programmes, terraces reducing net crop income, a Brazilian production-cistern programme with a benefit-cost ratio far below break-even, single SWC measures not covering their annual costs, and sand dams likely not cost-efficient [ev_food_security_abate21_4, ev_food_security_arega24_1, ev_household_income_mala24_1, ev_economic_return_casag22_9, ev_economic_return_zoug14_3, ev_economic_return_ritc21_1]. Compilers also rate check-dam land in China as raising the risk of production failure in extreme wet years and record no change on several sheets, including a subsistence farm pond in India; Kenyan sand dams sit inside a wider food-security programme, and food security, income and returns are all proxies for poverty [ev_food_security_wocat_1455_2011_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1474_2011_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1537_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Short-term returns on establishment are rated slightly to very negative on sheets from Tunisia, China, Rwanda, Yemen, Cabo Verde, Nicaragua, Jordan, Uzbekistan and Somalia, reflecting up-front costs that are only recovered over time. The Kenyan sand-dam income rise compares a small sample of households with a control catchment [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. New evidence adds further limits: the same synthesis reports negative net present values for graded fanya juu (−148 Birr per hectare) and graded soil bunds (−708 Birr per hectare), possibly because off-site benefits were left out [ev_economic_return_adim16_4]; cost savings from conservation agriculture are usually small for smallholders; and in a Kenyan drought season net benefits were higher without tied ridging [ev_economic_return_corb20_1, ev_economic_return_ndun23_1]. The Zimbabwe planting-basin margins include manure and fertiliser and the high-rainfall figure is a sensitivity scenario, the Indian pond returns are cross-sectional from a preprint survey confounded by farm size and assets, the reviewed income and water-value figures are secondary citations at their upper end, and the Peruvian income gain is modelled [ev_economic_return_mazv09_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_household_income_wei16_1]. In Malawi's El Nino season banking lowered the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement from 0.19 to 0.054, so a mis-timed in-field practice can cut food security rather than raise it [ev_food_security_boil19_3]. 30-cm zaï on the same Burkina Faso trial ran at a loss (−98 624 FCFA per hectare), smaller than the direct-seeding loss, and the investment counted is the experiment's own cost [ev_economic_return_zour25h1_4]. The Zimbabwe ratio is a single drought-season budget with the mulch bundled with no-till [ev_economic_return_mash25h1_3]. The teff returns are cited second-hand [ev_economic_return_tade23h1_4]. The Burkina Faso food-security statement is cited and does not separate manure from soil and water conservation [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5]. The Ethiopian income claim is cited from a study that the citing review itself describes as methodologically weak [ev_household_income_tade23h1_1]. The Zambian returns are crop budgets with output estimated from regression coefficients, bundled with early planting and purchased inputs (hybrid seed and fertiliser for maize), and the authors say early-planting gains dominate the maize results [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_hagg03_8]. The Zimbabwe panel figure is gross revenue at later market prices with labour and non-market inputs unvalued, so it is neither a profit nor a poverty measure [ev_economic_return_mich19_8]. The barraginha income and food-security findings are Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, from an informal survey and adopter ratings with no normal-year reference [ev_household_income_mira19_1, ev_food_security_mira19_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In semi-arid areas, production cisterns and subsurface dams let families irrigate gardens and fruit, diversifying diets and raising farm income, while zai and stone bunds raise cereal output and return to labour; food security rises with the area of farm under bunds.
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: Income gains from the Brazilian production-cistern programme are small and turned negative for larger farms, its benefit-cost ratio is well below one, and subsurface dams yielded little cash income in stagnant local economies; a Sahelian study found SWC families still in deficit in low-rainfall years, and single SWC measures did not repay annual costs.

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In mixed crop–livestock systems, farm budgets show water capture both paying and not paying. In Zimbabwe, planting-basin conservation farming earned a first-year maize gross margin of 473.36 against 70.6 US dollars per hectare for conventional practice without fertiliser and 48.19 with fertiliser, and experienced households could earn US$866.84 per hectare against US$357.16 for a farmer using chemical fertilizer in higher rainfall [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_3, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2]. In semi-arid India, net returns rose with livestock and trees to US$ 586 per hectare and to US$ 857 once a farm pond was added [ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. In a Kenyan highland trial, by contrast, net benefits in the short-rains season were higher without tied ridging than with it, except under one soil treatment [ev_economic_return_ndun23_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: The sides differ in season, in what is compared and in how cleanly water capture is isolated. The Kenyan loss is from a short-rains season of meteorological droughts, in a trial that compares tied ridging with and without under the same soil inputs [ev_economic_return_ndun23_1]; it is the cleanest single comparison here. The Zimbabwean gains set a package of basins, manure, fertiliser and residue against conventional practice, so the water-capture effect is mixed with nutrient supply, and the higher-rainfall figure is a sensitivity scenario with assumed yields [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2]. The Indian figure comes from a farmer survey in which few farms had a pond, the pond water was also used for irrigation, and the compared farms differ in other ways [ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. The evidence therefore cannot say whether water capture alone pays in this farming system; the gains belong to packages, and the one isolated test found a loss in a drought season. All of these are farm budgets rather than measures of household poverty, and none follows households over time [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2, ev_economic_return_mazv09_3, ev_economic_return_ndun23_1, ev_economic_return_pals23_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In the Brazilian semi-arid, cisterns and subsurface dams supply water for gardens, fruit and livestock, improving diets and raising family farm income, with the largest income effects on small farms; Andean terrace rehabilitation is judged to pay back through long durability.
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: Evidence is from upper-middle-income Brazil and Peru, outside the LIC/LMIC target band. A quasi-experimental study found modest income gains, no effect outside the Northeast, a negative effect on larger farms and a benefit-cost ratio far below one; several units are Embrapa or programme self-assessments and household self-reports.

water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and lines, banquettes, trenches, pits and check dams slow overland flow and spread it behind barriers, so less runoff leaves the slope and less soil is detached and carried away; check dams and gabions trap sediment in channels. Measured reductions are large: terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, Burundi terrace plots cut erosion by 50% to 90%, trenches reduced soil loss by 73.0% on average, and check dams cut catchment sediment export by 20 to 98% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_1, ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1]. WOCAT compilers across many countries rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as reduced, explaining that micro-catchments cut the kinetic energy of rain by trapping runoff and that check dams slow runoff so soil accumulates upstream [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_2895_2017_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_soil_loss]. Meta-analyses confirm the direction: a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds soil loss cut by 58.66% and runoff by 53% on average, with soil-loss reductions of 68.67% for mulching, 54.97% for ridging, 55.06% for soil and stone bunds and 60.21% for terraces [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_1, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_1, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_2, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_3, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_4, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_5]; an Ethiopian synthesis reports soil loss down 59% under graded soil bunds, 88% under level soil bunds, 38% under stone bunds, 98% under mulch and 62% under tied ridging [ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_1, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_2, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_3, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_4, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_5]; and a terracing meta-analysis finds erosion control on terraces 11.46 times that of controls and runoff reduction 2.6 times [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_1]. At catchment scale, stone bunds, check dams and regrowth in Ethiopia cut sediment yield from 8.5 to 1.9 t per hectare a year, and check dams on China's Loess Plateau reduced erosion rates from more than 200 to 20–25 t per hectare a year [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_luca21_1]. A meta-analysis of mulching finds runoff reduced by 47.4% and soil loss by 76.2% against controls, soil loss by 70.9% on cropland, and reductions of 45.9% and 75.1% at rainfall intensities above 90 mm/h [ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_1, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_2, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_3, ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_5, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_6]. In Brazil, barraginhas dispersed across farms capture runoff water, which Embrapa says prevents erosion, siltation and the carrying of pollutants [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.conditionality: Over two thirds of the pool are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets, and several literature sources are lender self-reports with before/after designs, perception surveys or catchment numbers that barely changed: the Rwanda sediment drop from 54 to 2.6 tons/ha a year has no control, and Indian sediment yield moved only from 71.6 to 69.3 tons per ha per year [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_utk22_3, ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5]; runoff reduction and sediment retention enter as component proxies. Negative findings: check dams can cause downstream channel incision, diversion banquettes increased gully and bank erosion in Niger, trenches raised sediment in the first years, Maghreb banquettes were often erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. Some sheets rate no change, including the Indian farm-pond sheet, and the Zambian tillage sheet expects less downstream siltation only if applied on a large scale [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_siltation]. A catchment-restoration meta-analysis in Ethiopia finds minimal effect of catchment treatment on runoff in drought-prone areas with annual rainfall below 500 mm [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_3]. In Tunisia gullied area on banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, poorly maintained banquettes in Algeria accelerate erosion, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]; and USA check dams had no significant effect on the runoff volume of major storms [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2]. The meta-analyses pool unweighted study means and are dominated by plot-scale East African studies, so catchment-scale effects remain less certain [ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1]. The mulching meta-analysis pools land uses including post-fire forest and bare land; cropland and tree crops were less effective in reducing runoff, both below 40%, and the mulching benefits decreased with increasing rainfall intensity under heavy rainfall [ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_4, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_6]. The barraginha erosion statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measurement [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.mechanism: In the Maghreb, contour structures have been reported both to hold runoff and to accelerate erosion. Staggered earth bunds (tabia) in Morocco store the runoff of all rains below 50 mm on the field [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. In Algeria, a poorly maintained banquette becomes a factor accelerating erosion, because the smallest unrepaired breach triggers a chain reaction through the whole network in torrential and prolonged rains [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.conditionality: Two conditions separate the sides in the sources. Maintenance: the acceleration is tied explicitly to unrepaired breaches in state-built banquettes [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2]. Storm size: the tabia hold runoff only up to rains of 50 mm, and in bigger storms the excess overtops them and gullies the whole slope [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. The actionable reading is to plan and fund upkeep and spillways, not only construction. Elsewhere banquettes simply did not stop gullying: gullied areas on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, and over 1947-1968 Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. Neither side is measured on plots: the protective statement is from an expert manual and the harmful ones are secondary citations within a national evaluation, and the two concern different structures, tabia and banquettes [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.mechanism: In high-income settings check dams and ponds trap sediment: loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland watersheds retained 48.4% and 82.4% of total sediment yield and halved outlet sediment per unit of peak runoff, four field-edge ponds in southern Germany trapped 54-85% of incoming sediment over 8 years, and a typical Belgian pond had a long-term trapping efficiency of 68% [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. Bench terracing in a small USA watershed reduced runoff by 9% and sediment yield by 58% [ev_runoff_reduction_meko14_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.conditionality: Check dams had no statistically significant effect on the runoff volume of major storms, reducing only the number of runoff events from small storms by 60%, and the halving of outlet sediment was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2, ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Check dams can also increase erosion downstream: channel incision was observed below 81% of surveyed check dams in a Spanish catchment [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1]. Most units are secondary citations in reviews, and the high-income settings (rangeland, arable fields with ponds) differ from smallholder water harvesting [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Tunisia, drought caused a shortfall in the spate-irrigation and water-recharge works established in Medenine, where only 15 were built against a target of 95 [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The single unit comes from an ex-post review drawing on project completion data and describes an establishment-phase shortfall of works, not physical damage to structures already built.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: On Ethiopian highland soil and water conservation structures, when the drainage ditch behind a bund fills with sediment, trapping efficiency quickly decreases and the extra pressure on the structure can lead to structural failure [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a single statement cited second-hand in a review of Ethiopian studies, with no rate or frequency of failure, and it implies the damage depends on whether the ditches are cleared [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Burkina Faso, soils on farms using soil and water conservation techniques had higher carbon and nitrogen contents than the control farm [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3], and a review cites climate-smart packages of soil and water conservation structures with biological measures boosting soil carbon stock by three to seven times over business-as-usual [ev_soil_organic_carbon_tade23h1_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Only two units, neither a measured stock change against a matched control: the Burkina Faso figure is a carbon content on farms using several techniques with compost, and the three-to-sevenfold gain is a review's citation of a package that includes biological measures, very large for structures and to be read with caution [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_tade23h1_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed-scale soil and water conservation is reported to raise groundwater, used here as a component of catchment water yield: stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale increase ground water level [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1]; in Burkina Faso improved well levels are linked to SWC measures that control surface runoff and improve infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]; ISRO survey data record an increase in groundwater recharge in treated areas in India [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3]; piezometers recorded groundwater levels rising in 16 of 21 non-desert districts with an average increase of 1.42 meters [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_3]; the Uttarakhand water budget shows aquifer recharge up 3.3 percent and water yield from catchment areas up 4.9 percent [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5]; and in Ethiopia improvements in the water table made small-scale irrigation possible [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_eth16_7]. In Burkina Faso, cited studies show soil and water conservation techniques improving the availability of ground water in many villages, especially large rock bunds known as digues filtrantes [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. Against the recharge reports, the downstream streamflow impacts of small-scale water storage systems have in other cases been limited, even when implemented widely [ev_water_yield_rock10_1]. The recharge gains have limits in their own sources: without data from untreated sites the Indian project impact is unclear [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3], subsidised tube-well pumping has possibly wiped out any increases in recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4], and in Burkina Faso the number of wells with water year round has not increased significantly [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]. The Uttarakhand figures are a modelled water budget [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5], and most other units are programme reports or cited statements; no unit compares downstream flow with and without catchment treatment. The digues filtrantes finding is cited from another study, with no figures [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Costs are the per-hectare unit cost of watershed treatments (bunds, check dams and other soil and water conservation works) across treated area in two World Bank-supported India watershed projects.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both figures come from one evaluation of bundled watershed programmes in India and are treatment costs per hectare treated, not per hectare of degraded land restored; the evaluator compares them with national budget norms rather than with outcomes.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Better-sited planning based on a land resource inventory avoided unnecessary structures, so construction of soil and water conservation works cost less per hectare than under the conventional integrated watershed programme.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Single lender completion-report figure from Karnataka, India, in local currency at stated price terms; the comparison is against another watershed programme, so it shows a saving from planning rather than the cost of SWC versus no SWC.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: These are programme-scale or unspecified soil and water conservation packages. A review of impact studies finds such methods particularly useful in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability, Ethiopia's PSNP public works improved watershed drought resilience by increasing water availability, and in semi-arid Brazil production cisterns can reduce animal mortality in severe drought [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. Physical soil and water conservation structures were also reported to buffer crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia, and a water-harvesting review states that dry spells can be bridged through investments in water management [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_1]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm and 1-m half-moon plots mitigated the impact of dry spells by retaining moisture for 2-3 weeks [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. A Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The same review states that crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought and different coping mechanisms are required [ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. The PSNP note adds that vegetation greenness still followed local drought severity, Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, and in Tunisia four consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. Every unit is a bundled programme, pooled soil and water conservation or an expert review, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated; the Brazilian statement describes potential without data and the Ethiopian 2015 finding is a secondary citation [ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]. The Burkina Faso half-moon and zaï moisture finding is the authors' statement about dry spells, for pits filled with compost [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. That Burkina Faso conclusion is the author's overall judgement, with no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: These are programme-scale or unspecified soil and water conservation packages. A review of impact studies finds such methods particularly useful in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability, Ethiopia's PSNP public works improved watershed drought resilience by increasing water availability, and in semi-arid Brazil production cisterns can reduce animal mortality in severe drought [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. Physical soil and water conservation structures were also reported to buffer crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia, and a water-harvesting review states that dry spells can be bridged through investments in water management [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_1]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm and 1-m half-moon plots mitigated the impact of dry spells by retaining moisture for 2-3 weeks [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. A Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The same review states that crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought and different coping mechanisms are required [ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. The PSNP note adds that vegetation greenness still followed local drought severity, Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, and in Tunisia four consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. Every unit is a bundled programme, pooled soil and water conservation or an expert review, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated; the Brazilian statement describes potential without data and the Ethiopian 2015 finding is a secondary citation [ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]. The Burkina Faso half-moon and zaï moisture finding is the authors' statement about dry spells, for pits filled with compost [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. That Burkina Faso conclusion is the author's overall judgement, with no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed works and production cisterns increase stored water, which improved watershed drought resilience in Ethiopia and can reduce livestock deaths in severe droughts in Brazil [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. A Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Ethiopian public-works study bundles area closures, small-scale irrigation and soil and water conservation, the Brazilian cistern statement is framed as a potential effect, and in Tunisia consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits (no benefit rather than damage); none quantifies drought impacts [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. That Burkina Faso conclusion is the author's overall judgement, with no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed programmes combining physical and vegetative barriers, bunds, check dams and terraces reduce runoff and soil loss: runoff dropped by 5 to 18 percent across Indian states, downstream runoff in the Karnataka catchments examined fell by 10 to 22 percent, and Ethiopian public works cut soil loss by 32.2% [ev_runoff_reduction_iegind11_6, ev_runoff_reduction_iegind11_5, ev_erosion_hazard_eth16_4, ev_erosion_hazard_arega24_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are bundled programme results measuring runoff or soil loss as proxies for flood impact, several from Bank completion reports or perception surveys, such as 84 percent of Ethiopian respondents reporting reduced run-off [ev_runoff_reduction_eth16_2, ev_erosion_hazard_eth16_4, ev_runoff_reduction_kar20_1]. Effects at watershed scale are small or absent: Karnataka project watersheds cut runoff by 3.2 percent against conventional sites, Uttarakhand sediment yield fell only from 71.6 to 69.3 tons per ha per year, and its water-budget model showed overall surface runoff up 1.5 percent [ev_runoff_reduction_kar20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_utk22_3, ev_runoff_reduction_utk22_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: A review of quasi-experimental studies reports that the impact of soil and water conservation is especially significant in areas with temperature shocks or lower rainfall [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is one narrative statement from a review that does not name specific practices, does not separate heat shocks from low rainfall and gives no magnitude; no unit measures heat-stress losses directly [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Soil and water conservation and water harvesting have been found both to raise and to lower production. Gains come from retaining moisture and soil: a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds a pooled yield gain of 71% over controls, with 69% for soil and stone bunds and gains of 71.7% for maize and 68.2% for sorghum without fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_tefe24_1, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_4, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_7, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_8]; four studies in a systematic review find 20–24 per cent gains in crop yield or value of production, particularly in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability [ev_crop_yield_mala24_1, ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_crop_yield_mala24_5]; zai pits combined with stone lines in Burkina Faso are reported to raise sorghum yields by over 100% [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_3]; Ethiopian early adopters had a 15.2 percent higher value of production and invested plots 20.6 percent higher [ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_1, ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_4]; physical structures buffered crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]; and dry spells can be bridged through water management [ev_crop_yield_rock10_1]. Programme reports add rainfed yield gains of 24% to 26% in Karnataka and 20.8% in Uttarakhand, yields rising from 0.5 to more than 1.2 t per hectare in wetter Mauritanian watersheds, and crop diversification from water harvesting with irrigation [ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1, ev_crop_yield_utk22_1, ev_crop_yield_mrt14_2, ev_agricultural_production_value_arega24_2]. Losses come from structures taking cropland and from excess water: in an Ethiopian synthesis fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare, bunds cut yields by up to 7% in the first few years, and rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively, possibly through waterlogging [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]; plots with bunds yielded less than non-conserved plots in high-rainfall western Amhara [ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_10]. A review cites soil and water conservation structures combined with biological measures raising wheat production by 30–45% over business-as-usual [ev_crop_yield_tade23h1_2]. Soils on Burkina Faso farms using soil and water conservation techniques had higher nitrogen contents than the control farm, used here as a component [ev_soil_nitrogen_sawa11h1_4].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The class is set by the gains. The excess-water losses are held out of it as a caveat on where the practice performs rather than as production evidence: annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively, which the synthesis puts down to water logging on the furrows of structures, fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare, and plots with bunds yielded less than non-conserved plots in high-rainfall western Amhara [ev_crop_yield_adim16_6, ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_10]. Bunds should not be applied where rainfall is that heavy. The evidence itself names what separates gains from losses. Rainfall: gains concentrate in low-rainfall or variable areas and in drier periods, while bunds lose yield in high-rainfall areas, and in Tigray bunds slightly raised productivity in drier periods but reduced it in moist seasons because cropped area was lost to the bunds [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_10, ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_8, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]. Time and maintenance: value of production rose only after structures had been maintained for at least 7 years, later adopters saw no significant gain, and bunds cut yields in the first few years [ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_5, ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7]. Who decides: imposed structures often reduced cultivable area by 3 to 20% without improving productivity, and structures promoted mostly off-farm for community resource protection gave no gain [ev_crop_yield_roose94_5, ev_crop_yield_abate21_1].
