water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for zaï or tassa pits and contour bunds in Niger rate wind velocity as reduced [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1219_2014_wind_velocity, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1652_2014_wind_velocity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: These are practitioner ratings without stated reasoning, and the Philippine conservation-tillage compiler rates wind velocity as unchanged [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1021_2011_wind_velocity]. No unit addresses cyclone or storm damage directly.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for Nardi or Vallerani trenches and semi-circular bunds in Niger rate both technologies as coping well with drought [ev_asset_drought_wocat_1613_2014_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1614_2014_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings from Niger with no observed damage data, so the row reflects compiler judgement for a single country.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate Nardi or Vallerani trenches and semi-circular bunds in Niger as not coping well with local rainstorms and the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso as coping moderately [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1613_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1614_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1528_2012_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: These are practitioner ratings without damage records, and the compiler for mechanised Vallerani harvesting in Jordan rates coping as very good, so the outcome may depend on setting [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5860_2021_local_rainstorm].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate Vallerani and Nardi trenches and semi-circular bunds in Burkina Faso and Niger as not coping well with floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1528_2012_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1613_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1614_2014_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: These are practitioner ratings without damage records, and the compiler for mechanised Vallerani harvesting in Jordan rates coping with flash floods as very good, so the outcome may depend on setting [ev_asset_flood_wocat_5860_2021_flash_flood].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan rates the technology as coping very well with extreme winter conditions [ev_asset_frost_wocat_5860_2021_extreme_winter_conditions].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating with no observed damage [ev_asset_frost_wocat_5860_2021_extreme_winter_conditions].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Burkina Faso the 2- and 3-m half-moon plots showed lower infiltration than the control plots, likely due to suspended matter that clogs the soil during sedimentation [ev_soil_permeability_zour25h1_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is one source and one trial, and the finding is for the larger (2- and 3-m) half-moons only. The authors give sedimentation as the likely cause without testing it, and the damage is reduced infiltration capacity inside the basin rather than a breach or loss of the structure [ev_soil_permeability_zour25h1_8].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate Nardi or Vallerani trenches and semi-circular bunds in Niger as coping well with local windstorms, and the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso as coping very well [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1613_2014_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1614_2014_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1528_2012_local_windstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: For the Vallerani System of tractor-ploughed micro-catchments in Burkina Faso, the WOCAT compiler reports floral diversity rising from 14 to 44 species with a high share of good forage grasses and the return of more leguminous species, and insects, birds, reptiles and mammals observed on implemented sites [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1528_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1528_2012_animal_diversity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units come from a single technology sheet, with no independent ecological measurement or untreated comparison, and no other source or country is covered.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: For the Vallerani System in Burkina Faso, the WOCAT compiler reports biomass production 5 to 30 times that of nearby unploughed soil and rates emissions as reduced because ploughing produces minimal carbon dioxide relative to the gain; soil organic matter is rated increased there and under mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1528_2012_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1528_2012_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1528_2012_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5860_2021_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C]. A Chinese meta-analysis, available as a preprint, reports fish-scale pits raising soil organic carbon storage by 79.86% on the Loess Plateau in years 11~30 [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_12].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets covering essentially the same Vallerani technique, with no measured carbon stock change; biomass and soil organic matter stand in for sequestration, and the soil organic matter ratings carry no compiler comment. The fish-scale-pit figure is from a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, is an abstract statement for the best duration window in an upper-middle-income country, and is the only measured unit in this row [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_12].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The only per-hectare cost for the micro-catchment family is the compiler's cost table for mechanised Vallerani trenching in Jordan, costed per hectare [ev_project_cost_wocat_5860_2021_establishment].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single practitioner-reported figure from an upper-middle-income country, outside the target band, so it informs the family row but not the low- and lower-middle-income class [ev_project_cost_wocat_5860_2021_establishment].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The Burkina Faso WOCAT compiler links increased vegetation cover, deep roots and water storage in the soil profile to drought resilience, reporting that in years of extreme drought plants reduced their growth but most survived and grew again in the following rainy season [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row rests on a single WOCAT compiler rating from one technology sheet, not a measured comparison, and the same compiler notes that growth still fell in extreme drought years [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The compiler of the WOCAT sheet on the Vallerani System in Burkina Faso judges that greater biodiversity, vegetation cover and soil fertility, deep root systems and water stored in the soil profile increase resilience to drought.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single practitioner judgement from a technology sheet, not a measured drought outcome.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The Vallerani compiler in Burkina Faso keeps the treated area open to regulated grazing to reduce the grass growth that could favour the spread of fire, and herders monitor the area [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_fire_risk].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row rests on a single WOCAT compiler rating, a practitioner judgement rather than a measurement, and the reduction it describes comes from grazing management alongside the micro-catchments rather than from the basins themselves [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_fire_risk].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Micro-catchments retain rain where it falls, so the Burkina Faso compiler reports that flood risk decreases, and compilers in Niger and Jordan rate downstream flooding and flood impacts as reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1613_2014_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1614_2014_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_flood_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a WOCAT compiler rating rather than a measurement. The Burkina Faso compiler adds that a flood in the ploughed area before vegetation is well established can wash out the micro basins [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_flood_impacts].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Through water harvesting the rain is retained where it falls and flood risk decreases, as the compiler of the Vallerani System sheet in Burkina Faso puts it; compilers for Nardi/Vallerani trenches and semi-circular bunds in Niger and Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan also judge flood impacts and downstream flooding reduced.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets with no hydrological measurement, and the Burkina Faso compiler cautions that a flood on ploughed land before vegetation is established can wash out the micro basins.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Semi-circular bunds, Vallerani micro-catchments and trenches harvest runoff for crops and grasses: WOCAT compilers report crop production and biomass augmented several times over traditional techniques with the Vallerani System in Burkina Faso, higher millet and straw yields from cropland bunds on abandoned farmland in Niger, and more fodder and grazing days. Negarim micro-catchments with supplementary irrigation supported fruit production at Embrapa Semi-Arid in Brazil, and semi-circular bunds raised millet grain production under African conditions. A review tabulates crop yield increases of 50–200% from half-moons in Burkina Faso and Niger, and cites micro-basin water harvesting in Zambia doubling maize yields to 3 t per hectare [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_2, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_5]. On crusted degraded soil in Burkina Faso, 1-m half-moons with compost gave 1372 kg of millet per hectare where direct seeding gave none [ev_crop_yield_zour25h1_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Apart from an FAO manual citing earlier work and a review quoting ranges from earlier studies, all units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, not measurements. Animal production was rated lower for trenches and semi-circular bunds in Niger because treated rangeland must be protected from grazing for the first years while vegetation establishes. The review figures are ranges and single citations rather than pooled estimates [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_2, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_5]. The Burkina Faso zaï and half-moon contrasts are against land where direct seeding produced no grain, with compost added to the pits, so they measure bringing degraded land into production rather than an improvement on a cropped field. It is the one measured unit in this row [ev_crop_yield_zour25h1_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Vallerani tractor-ploughed micro-catchments, Nardi/Vallerani trenches and semi-circular bunds collect runoff for sown fodder and crops; the Burkina Faso compiler links more and better fodder to improved animal health, productivity and market price, and deep-rooted sown plants to a lower risk of production failure [ev_household_income_wocat_1528_2012_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1528_2012_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_1528_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Sheets for Niger rate food self-sufficiency and farm income as greatly increased [ev_food_security_wocat_1613_2014_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1614_2014_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_wocat_1613_2014_farm_income]. Compilers mostly rate benefits as outweighing establishment and maintenance costs, especially over the long term. On crusted degraded soil in Burkina Faso, 1-m half-moons with compost were profitable at 377 275 FCFA per hectare after the investment [ev_economic_return_zour25h1_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner rating from a WOCAT technology sheet; no literature unit measures income or food security for these practices. The Jordan sheet rates only a slight gain in food self-sufficiency and a slightly negative short-term return on establishment, and food security and farm income are proxies for poverty [ev_food_security_wocat_5860_2021_food_security_selfsufficiency]. The half-moon profit is the one literature unit here; it comes from a trial on degraded land where the authors count the experiment's own investment [ev_economic_return_zour25h1_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Micro-catchments, Vallerani tractor-ploughed basins, Nardi/Vallerani trenches and semi-circular bunds trap runoff in small basins, which the Kenyan compiler says cuts the kinetic energy of rainwater and so reduces soil loss; the Burkina Faso sheet adds that ploughing along the contour collects runoff between the tilled lines and that wind erosion falls too [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_2895_2017_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1528_2012_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_soil_loss]. Sheets for Niger and Jordan rate soil loss and surface runoff as reduced [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1613_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_soil_loss].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner rating from a WOCAT technology sheet; no literature measurement covers this family. The semi-circular bund sheet for Niger rates downstream siltation unchanged, so the off-site sediment benefit rests on the Jordan rating alone [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1614_2014_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5860_2021_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The Jordan sheet for mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting rates downstream siltation as reduced, consistent with runoff and sediment being held in the micro-basins [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5860_2021_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Only practitioner ratings support this cell, and the semi-circular bund sheet for Niger rates downstream siltation unchanged [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1614_2014_downstream_siltation]. Siltation is a component proxy for water quality; no water-quality measurement exists for this family.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Micro-basins, trenches and semi-circular bunds capture rain and runoff from the surrounding bare soil and hold it long enough to infiltrate the soil profile and eventually the water table; the compiler for the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso relays local people's reports that well levels rose after implementation [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1528_2012_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1528_2012_water_availability]. Compilers for Nardi/Vallerani trenches and semi-circular bunds in Niger and mechanised Vallerani ploughing in Jordan judge the technologies to improve water harvesting [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1613_2014_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1614_2014_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5860_2021_harvesting_collection_of_water].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements from documented technology sheets, and the well-level rise is a second-hand community report rather than a measurement. The compiler for semi-circular bunds in Niger judges no change in water availability, so the gains mainly concern water captured in the field [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1614_2014_water_availability].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for mechanised micro water harvesting in Jordan rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row rests on a single compiler rating with no comment or measurement, from an upper-middle-income country outside the target band, and it concerns rain-storm impacts rather than wind [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Rooftop storage depends on rain to refill: in great multi-year droughts the domestic cistern runs dry and households fall back on water trucks, and WOCAT compilers for rooftop systems in Nepal and Uganda rate the technology as not coping well with drought [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1497_2011_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1595_2013_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a functional failure of storage rather than structural damage; the Brazilian unit is an implementer interview and the others are practitioner ratings, none quantified [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate rooftop rainwater systems in Nepal and Uganda as coping well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1497_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1595_2013_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without observed damage or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate rooftop rainwater systems in Nepal and Uganda as coping well with river floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1497_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1595_2013_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without damage records or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate rooftop rainwater systems in Nepal and Uganda as coping well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1497_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1595_2013_local_windstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without observed damage or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The compiler of a WOCAT sheet on Rubagano rooftop rainwater harvesting with a concrete or brick tank in Uganda rated plant diversity slightly increased; the sheet gives no mechanism.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single practitioner judgement without comment or measurement; the link from roof-water storage to wider plant diversity is not explained in the source, so the row is indicative only.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Domestic rooftop cisterns in semi-arid Brazil store rainwater for the dry period, giving households basic drinking and cooking water near the home, cutting the time spent fetching water and postponing or avoiding the shortages that send families to water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4]. In a survey of beneficiary families, 57.8% said the cistern fully met drinking, cooking and personal hygiene needs, and the WOCAT compiler for a rooftop tank system in Uganda rates water quantity and availability as improved [ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1595_2013_water_quantity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The benefit is set by storage per person: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, larger households stay dependent on water trucks, and only 19.1% of surveyed families named the cistern as their main source [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2]. In great multi-year droughts the cisterns run dry and households fall back on water trucks, which records no benefit at that point rather than damage to the tank [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3]. The survey used recall with no control group, the other Brazilian units are implementer or author statements, and the Ugandan units are practitioner ratings; all describe domestic water access as a component proxy, not crop or livestock losses [ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Domestic cisterns in semi-arid Brazil store rainwater for the dry season, but in great multi-year droughts they run dry and households fall back on water trucks, leaving them very vulnerable [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a single expert statement from a Brazilian programme account, upper-middle-income and adjacent to the target; it records no drought benefit once storage is exhausted, a benefit shortfall rather than damage to the tank, and says nothing about shorter droughts.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The pooled cost is the average construction cost of a roof rainwater-harvesting tank under the Himachal Pradesh mid-Himalayan watershed project in India, reported per structure from the project's output table.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single lender completion report, self-reported from physical and financial monitoring; the figure is a nominal rupee average over the project years converted at one exchange rate, so it indicates the order of cost of a household tank rather than a transferable unit rate.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Rooftop tanks capture part of the rain falling on roofs; the WOCAT compiler for a rooftop system with a concrete or brick tank in Uganda rates surface runoff and downstream flooding as reduced [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1595_2013_surface_runoff, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1595_2013_downstream_flooding].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both sheets are practitioner ratings, and the Nepal compiler rates downstream flooding as unchanged because only a little portion of rainfall is trapped from the roof [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_flooding].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Rooftop systems trap part of the rainfall from roofs, and the compiler for Rubagano rooftop harvesting with a concrete or brick tank in Uganda judged downstream flooding slightly reduced.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Only practitioner judgements from technology sheets; the Nepal compiler rated the effect neutral because only a little rainfall is trapped from the roof, so any flood benefit is marginal.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The only unit is the compiler's rating on the WOCAT sheet for the Rubagano rooftop rainwater harvesting system with a concrete or brick tank in Uganda, which records crop production as increased; the sheet gives no comment on how the stored roof water reaches crops [ev_crop_yield_wocat_1595_2013_crop_production].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a practitioner judgement from a documented technology sheet, not a measured yield, and no literature unit supports it; whether the rating holds beyond this single Ugandan technology is untested [ev_crop_yield_wocat_1595_2013_crop_production].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The Ugandan Rubagano rooftop system's WOCAT sheet rates farm income and food self-sufficiency as increased [ev_household_income_wocat_1595_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1595_2013_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In Brazil, domestic cisterns fully met family drinking and household needs for many households and improved quality of life and health, but did not influence income [ev_household_income_silva09_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The signals point in different directions: a Brazilian household survey from an upper-middle-income setting finds no income effect, while the Ugandan input is a single compiler's ratings that also record the risk of production failure as unchanged [ev_household_income_silva09_3, ev_food_security_wocat_1595_2013_risk_of_production_failure]. Neither source measures income change, and the Brazilian null concerns cash income rather than other welfare outcomes.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Capturing roof runoff in a tank keeps it off the ground around the homestead: the Ugandan Rubagano sheet rates surface runoff as reduced, and the Nepali compiler notes less eroded material from the courtyard [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1595_2013_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings, and the Nepali sheet rates downstream siltation unchanged despite its comment, so any effect is confined to the homestead and is not measured [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation]. Runoff reduction and sediment retention enter only as component proxies for soil erosion.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The Nepali rooftop rainwater harvesting sheet rates downstream siltation unchanged, while its compiler notes less eroded material from the courtyard [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This rests on a single practitioner rating of downstream siltation, a component proxy; it says nothing about the quality of the stored water itself [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Domestic rooftop cisterns store rainwater beside the house, giving households basic drinking and cooking water through the dry season, sharply reducing time spent fetching water and dependence on water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4]. The Ugandan Rubagano sheet rates water quantity as greatly increased [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1595_2013_water_quantity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most units come from cistern programmes in Brazil (upper-middle income), largely programme authors and household surveys. A standard cistern covers basic needs only for small households, larger families remain dependent on water trucks, and most households still use other sources as their main supply [ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2]. The Ugandan sheet rates overall water availability only slightly improved [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1595_2013_water_availability].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Subsurface dams in semi-arid Brazil tended to dry out during a year without rain, and small manually built dams do not withstand long droughts, limiting production through dry spells [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. WOCAT compilers rate check dams in China, Nepal and India and sand dams in Kenya as coping well with drought, and a haffir and gabion check dams in Somalia as coping moderately [ev_asset_drought_wocat_1455_2011_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1537_2012_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_7777_2026_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Brazilian units describe storage exhaustion rather than structural damage, and the rest are practitioner ratings of coping without observed failure data [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: A check-dam review notes that examples of check dams failing to meet their objectives are common worldwide and are often associated with structure failure in extreme rainfall events or lack of maintenance [ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av]. Among runoff-catchment works, the WOCAT compiler for gully-plugging check dams in Nepal judges them not to cope well with local rainstorms, and gabions and rock check dams in Somalia are rated as coping only moderately with rainstorms and thunderstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1493_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_7778_2026_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_7778_2026_local_thunderstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Gabion check dams in Tunisia, check dams in China, sand dams in Kenya and stone check walls and check dams in India are judged to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1400_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1455_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1537_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5210_2019_local_rainstorm]; vegetative check dams (fascines) in Madagascar cope well with rainstorms and thunderstorms but moderately with hailstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6478_2022_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6478_2022_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6478_2022_local_hailstorm]. The review statement does not separate rainfall damage from neglect, and the rest are WOCAT compiler ratings, not measured damage [ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for stone check walls and check dams in India rates the technology as coping well with forest fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5210_2019_forest_fire].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating with no observed damage or stated reasoning [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5210_2019_forest_fire].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Floods washed away scores of small dams in northern Ghana, 37.9% of boulder-faced log check dams in Ethiopia still failed after a high-magnitude runoff event, and when peak flows break check dams the stored sediment is released rapidly [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1]. A check-dam review cites structural failure from the impact of large boulders in extreme floods, and grassed earth gully check dams in Morocco are described as fragile during major floods and needing frequent winter maintenance [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1_av, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av]. WOCAT compilers rate gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and check-dam ponds in Ethiopia as not coping well with floods and a haffir and gabion check dams in Somalia as coping moderately [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1493_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1547_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7777_2026_flash_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Other compilers rate check dams in Tunisia, China and India and sand dams in Kenya as coping well, and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia as coping very well with flash floods, so sensitivity varies with construction, and the Moroccan earth check dams depend on frequent maintenance [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1400_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1537_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6716_2023_flash_flood, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av]. The check-dam failure and boulder-impact evidence is cited from other studies, the sediment-release statement comes from a USA study, the Ghana finding gives no count of dams lost, and the ratings are practitioner judgements [ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1_av, ev_flood_damage_veno12_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for gabions and rock check dams in Somalia rates the technology as coping moderately with heatwaves [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating with no stated reason or observed damage [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Stone check walls and check dams in India are rated by their WOCAT compiler as coping moderately with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5210_2019_landslide], and a double-basin masonry check dam in Ethiopia as coping well [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6716_2023_landslide].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This rests on just these compiler ratings from technology sheets; neither reports how a landslide would damage the structure, so there is no measured evidence on landslide damage to runoff-catchment works [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5210_2019_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6716_2023_landslide].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Reservoirs, tanks and dams trap the sediment that runoff carries, so storage fills and function declines: Tigray dams with a 30-year design life were set to run their cycle in 4.4 to 5.7 years, eight of ten Zambian reservoirs lost storage to siltation, 31 percent of earthen dams in Haryana silted up within five years, Moroccan gabions had nearly lost their original function, and small hill dams in Morocco lose 0.5 to 1% of capacity each year to catchment erosion [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_1, ev_asset_siltation_saru19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_iegind11_12, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2, ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av]. Loose-rock check dams on semi-arid rangeland watersheds in the USA were filled to more than 80% of capacity within four years, and a review notes the sediment-control effect of check dams diminishes as they fill and becomes marginal a few years to a few decades after installation [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1_av]. Sedimentation is described as perhaps the primary reason for sand dam failure, and tanks desilted in an Indian programme need desilting again within its lifetime [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3, ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Severity varies: a Kenyan sand-dam assessment estimates siltation cut storage by 10-25% and judges it neither an inherent limitation nor the main reason dams go unused [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. Most units are review citations or narrative observations without a common metric, the only directly measured fill rate comes from a high-income rangeland study, and losses depend on upkeep, as the Moroccan structures failed where no maintenance system had been put in place and small hill dams were forgotten once built [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_2, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2, ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate check dams in China and Nepal and sand dams in Kenya as coping well with local windstorms and gabion check dams in Somalia as coping moderately, while fascine (vegetative) check dams in Madagascar are rated as not coping well with tropical storms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1455_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1537_2012_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_7778_2026_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_6478_2022_tropical_storm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage; the Madagascar sheet alone rates tropical storms, and it concerns a vegetative structure rather than stone or concrete [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_6478_2022_tropical_storm].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers judge that water stored by runoff structures supports plant growth and habitat: on-farm ponds in Cambodia make water available for plants, sand dams in Kenya rejuvenate riverine ecologies and enable indigenous tree planting, and gabions and rock check dams in Somalia improved soil moisture, reduced erosion and restored vegetation, creating habitat for livestock and small wildlife [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_2844_2017_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1537_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_habitat_diversity]. Users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive greener surroundings and improved biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_veno12_1]. Embrapa reports that crops, vegetable gardens and orchards on the humid fringes of its barraginhas in Brazil bring back fauna that had disappeared for lack of food [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Apart from the Ghana user-perception statement, all units are compiler ratings from technology sheets in Kenya, Cambodia, Ethiopia and Somalia, mostly rated as slight change and several from the same sheet; the Ethiopian check-dam comment gives no mechanism, and no unit measures species or habitat [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6716_2023_plant_diversity]. The Brazilian barraginha fauna finding is an adopter-reported indicator in Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no species measured [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers judge that gabions and rock check dams in Somalia increase vegetation, above-ground biomass and soil organic matter through vegetation recovery and sediment accumulation, that a haffir in Somalia does so as vegetation cover regenerates, that tree cover at a masonry check dam in Ethiopia reduces emissions over time, and that tree nurseries enabled by sand dams in Kenya store carbon and reduce deforestation [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7778_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7777_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_6716_2023_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1537_2012_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. A check-dam review cites check dams on China's Loess Plateau contributing to carbon sequestration, an effect that grows with time at both dam and watershed level as sediment accumulates [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Apart from the Loess Plateau check-dam finding, which is a secondary citation in a review with no magnitude in the quoted passage, all units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, all rated slight, with no measured carbon; biomass, soil organic matter and avoided-emission ratings are proxies for sequestration, and several units come from the same Somali sheet [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_biomass_above_ground_C].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Check dams and sand dams recharge local groundwater: the proportion of runoff infiltrated through check dams can reach more than 50%, with recharge linked to episodic storm events [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_luca21_1]; groundwater tables rise in the vicinity of filled check dams [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_fran21_1]; sand dams can raise the local groundwater [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1]; in India additional recharge from check dams and other water harvesting structures was estimated at 480 million cubic meters per annum, contributing to post-monsoon stabilization of groundwater levels, and a state survey found groundwater levels increased in 22 of the 31 districts [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_2]; and a review lists aquifer recharge among benefits cited for water harvesting [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_saru19_1]. On the other side, on China's Loess Plateau, a large campaign of check-dam construction carried out since the 1970s to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments reduced streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. Embrapa says its barraginhas in Brazil help recharge groundwater by raising the water table and revitalise springs and rivers [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. Both sides involve check dams but measure different things: recharge and water tables at or near the structures, against streamflow below a campaign of check dams built at very large scale to retain floodwater. The gain is local and the sand-dam effect is often limited in space and time [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1]. Every unit is a secondary citation in a review or report, the Indian recharge figure is an estimate [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_1], and the 39% is a figure the review cites from another study [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]; no unit compares downstream flow with and without the works. water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for stone check walls and check dams in India rates fire risk as reduced, but the sheet gives no explanation of how the structures do this [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_fire_risk].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small reservoirs, sand dams, check dams and haffirs store or slow runoff: users of small reservoirs in northern Ghana list limiting rainy-season floods among their benefits, the Kenyan compiler notes a dam or series of dams buffers downstream flooding, the Ethiopian compiler that the structure and rehabilitated areas reduce downstream flooding, and the Somali compiler that stone lines, gabions and rock check dams reduced runoff velocity and flood-related erosion [ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts]. Size can reverse the effect: larger sand dams increase the risk of flooding, erosion and seepage [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1]. water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sand dams, small reservoirs, subsurface dams, farm ponds, check dams and haffirs store runoff that farmers use to irrigate more land and take a second or dry-season crop, while sediment trapped behind check dams can be planted with fodder; in Kenya sand-dam water lets farmers irrigate more crops and raise production, and in Brazil soil management in subsurface dams raised crop productivity [ev_crop_yield_ritc21_1, ev_crop_yield_brito07_5, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1474_2011_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_2844_2017_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_6716_2023_fodder_production]. WOCAT compilers in Somalia describe reliable irrigation from a haffir improving tomato and watermelon, grasses regenerating around the dam, and better water and fodder raising animal production [ev_crop_yield_wocat_7777_2026_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_7777_2026_fodder_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_7777_2026_animal_production]. Sand dams in Kenya cut crop failure against a control catchment, and in Zimbabwe improved water availability improved livestock health where cattle had been driven up to 20 km to water [ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1, ev_livestock_productivity_lazurko24_1]. Stored water also stabilises output: Indian farmers reported crop-failure chances falling from 20% to 6% in the rainy season and from 100% to 5–10% in winter with a farm pond, reviews report rainwater harvesting systems stabilising production under intra-seasonal rainfall variability and supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells, wheat output in Pakistan rose from 450 to 815 kg over seven years after small reservoirs were built, a bundle of moisture conservation, rainwater harvesting and micro-irrigation in India raised system productivity by 25%, and silt farmland behind check dams on China's Loess Plateau yields 6–10 times more than sloping farmland [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_yield_stability_pals23_2, ev_yield_stability_silv26_1, ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_1, ev_agricultural_production_value_silv26_1, ev_crop_yield_luca21_1]. In Rwanda, runoff from the terrace waterways collected in a dug, lined pond and applied to maize by a gravity drip kit as supplementary irrigation gave 11982 kg per hectare against 4755 on flat rainfed plots [ev_crop_yield_uwiz18h1_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT technology sheets, and the literature units are largely reviews citing earlier studies, an expert's personal communication on livestock, and Brazilian case accounts from an upper-middle-income setting [ev_crop_yield_ritc21_1, ev_livestock_productivity_veno12_1, ev_crop_yield_cirilo03_4]. A Brazilian subsurface dam produced no harvest in a year of adverse weather, and an Indian farm-pond sheet rates fodder production unchanged; fodder and livestock outcomes enter only as components of the production gap [ev_crop_yield_brito07_6, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1474_2011_fodder_production]. The Kenyan and Zimbabwean sand-dam findings come from interviews and respondent statements [ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1, ev_livestock_productivity_lazurko24_1]. Soil salinisation may appear on check-dam farmland, the Pakistani wheat figure has no area denominator, the Indian productivity gain bundles micro-irrigation, and the pond figures come from a farmer survey reported in a preprint [ev_crop_yield_luca21_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_1, ev_agricultural_production_value_silv26_1, ev_yield_stability_pals23_2]. The Rwandan pond result is a bundle — terrace runoff capture, a lined storage pond and drip irrigation — so the yield is delivered through irrigation hardware and cannot be read as a pure capture effect; it is one season of a randomised trial in which every plot received farmyard manure and mineral fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_uwiz18h1_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled costs are compiler-reported annual maintenance costs from WOCAT technology sheets: per structure for a farm pond with irrigation system in Cambodia, check dams and walls in India, a fascine line in Madagascar and a haffir in Somalia, and per hectare for sheets in India and Somalia (the Somalia sheet spreading its total over 160 ha).
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables for the documented technology, summed and converted to USD with the sheet's own exchange rate; they are not market prices. The cost class is set from the per-structure figures while the value range is per hectare, and structures range from a short fascine line to a large haffir, so neither summary is a comparable unit cost.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small reservoirs, sand dams, farm ponds, runoff cisterns and subsurface dams provide water for dry-season irrigation of vegetables and fruit and for livestock, shifting cropping towards higher-value crops and raising household income and lean-season food security [ev_household_income_veno12_2, ev_household_income_ritc21_3, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6]. WOCAT compilers add that farm ponds in Cambodia keep enough irrigation water through drought, gully check dams in Ethiopia free rangeland for grazing, and gully rehabilitation in Somalia raised crop and livestock productivity [ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6716_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_7778_2026_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Compilers' benefit-versus-cost ratings are positive or very positive over the long term for every sheet that rates them. In Kenya, farmers living near sand dams saw average income rise by 60% as more water in dry periods raised farm yields [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. Reviews add that rainwater-harvesting ponds brought statistically significant gains in household income and food security in Burkina Faso, water storage gave Ethiopian smallholders greater income security, harvested water used with precision irrigation in Ethiopia reached a net water value of up to 1.53 USD per cubic metre, and benefit-cost ratios of up to 3.38 with payback periods of 6.8 to 12 years; Indian farms with a farm pond reported net returns of 857 USD per hectare against 586 without [ev_household_income_silv26_1, ev_household_income_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_silv26_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. In Brazil, an Embrapa survey of some communities found small-farm incomes rose by about half a minimum wage per month after the second filling of the barraginhas, and adopters rated food security as the technology's largest impact [ev_household_income_mira19_1, ev_food_security_mira19_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most literature magnitudes are secondary citations in reviews or vote counts, and practitioner ratings make up a large share of the pool [ev_household_income_saru19_3, ev_household_income_veno12_3]. Sand dams are judged likely not cost-efficient for water supply, Brazilian subsurface dams produced little cash income where electricity, investment capital or an irrigation tradition were missing, and the high Brazilian benefit-cost ratios come from an upper-middle-income context [ev_economic_return_ritc21_1, ev_household_income_cirilo03_7, ev_economic_return_cirilo03_10]. Compilers rate check-dam land in China as raising the risk of production failure in extreme wet years and an Indian subsistence farm pond as leaving farm income unchanged; Kenyan sand dams are embedded in a wider food-security programme [ev_food_security_wocat_1455_2011_risk_of_production_failure, ev_household_income_wocat_1474_2011_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1537_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Short-term returns on establishment are rated slightly to very negative on sheets from Tunisia, China, Nicaragua and Somalia, and the cost-benefit units are compiler judgements, not measured returns. The Kenyan sand-dam income rise compares a small sample of households with a control catchment [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. The reviewed income, water-value and benefit-cost figures are secondary citations, reported at their upper end, and the Indian pond returns come from a cross-sectional preprint survey confounded by farm size and assets [ev_economic_return_silv26_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. The barraginha income and food-security findings are Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, from an informal survey and adopter ratings with no normal-year reference [ev_household_income_mira19_1, ev_food_security_mira19_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Check dams, gabions, fascines and gully plugs trap sediment in gullies and channels, reducing catchment sediment export, and hill reservoirs reduce outlet flows [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_4]. WOCAT compilers describe masonry check dams in Ethiopia slowing runoff so soil accumulates upstream, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia cutting runoff speed and gully expansion, and vegetative check dams in Madagascar reducing siltation of downstream rice fields [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7778_2026_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6478_2022_downstream_siltation]. Check dams on China's Loess Plateau reduced erosion rates from more than 200 to 20–25 t per hectare a year and cut regional runoff and sediment by about 15% and 85%, check dams at the outlets of five Chinese catchments accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction over 26 years, vegetated check dams in northern Ethiopia significantly reduced peak flow and runoff volume, loose-rock check dams on USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of sediment yield, and small ponds in Germany and Belgium trapped 54-85% and 68% of incoming sediment [ev_erosion_hazard_luca21_1, ev_runoff_reduction_luca21_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_runoff_reduction_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. In Brazil, barraginhas dispersed across farms capture runoff water, which Embrapa says prevents erosion, siltation and the carrying of pollutants [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most units are practitioner ratings; the pooled sediment figures come from a single check-dam synthesis, so the independent literature base is narrow [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_fran21_3]. Check dams can cause downstream channel incision through the clear-water effect (documented in Spain, a high-income setting), gabions in Morocco have filled and need raising to keep working, an Indian sheet rates soil loss unchanged, and the Ethiopian compiler notes that the visible siltation held back has not been quantified [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_siltation]. USA check dams had no significant effect on the runoff volume of major storms and their reduction of outlet sediment was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]; the Chinese, Ethiopian and European figures are secondary citations in reviews, and the USA and European sites are high-income [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_1]. The barraginha erosion statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measurement [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Check dams, gabions, fascines and gully plugs store sediment in channels, reducing catchment sediment yield and the topsoil washed downstream [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1]. WOCAT compilers rate downstream siltation as reduced, from stem-cutting check dams in Nicaragua and stone check walls in India to gabions and check dams in Somalia that trap sediment upstream of fields and water bodies, and gully plugs in Nepal that cut siltation into an irrigation canal [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1719_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5210_2019_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1493_2011_downstream_siltation]. In the literature check dams on China's Loess Plateau are credited with cutting regional sediment export by about 85% and accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction at the outlets of five catchments over 26 years, and loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of watershed sediment yield [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1], and small ponds trapped 54-85% of incoming sediment over 8 years in southern Germany and 68% over the long term in Belgium [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Sediment retention is a component proxy for water quality, and most units are practitioner ratings; the earlier literature magnitudes came from a single check-dam synthesis, and gabions in Morocco have filled up and need raising to keep trapping sediment [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1]. Sheets for olive runoff furrows in Syria, a gabion check dam in Tunisia and check-dam ponds in Ethiopia rate only a slight reduction [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1005_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1400_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1547_2012_downstream_siltation]. The added figures are mostly secondary citations in reviews, the USA, German and Belgian sites are high-income, and the USA halving of outlet sediment was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sand dams, check dams, subsurface dams, ponds and production cisterns store water in sand, soil or tanks and recharge local groundwater, extending the months of water access and keeping livestock watered when other sources dry up. WOCAT compilers for gabion check dams in Tunisia, check dam ponds and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia, sand dams in Kenya, stone check walls in India, on-farm ponds in Cambodia and a haffir and gabion check dams in Somalia judge them to improve water harvesting, quantity or availability [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1400_2011_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1547_2012_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_2844_2017_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7777_2026_harvesting_collection_of_water]. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1]. A check-dam review reports that check dams storing seasonal runoff solve local supply scarcity; traditional rainwater ponds in South Korea reduced the occurrence of water deficit from 30 to 20% [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Many Kenyan sand dams lack capacity to supply even one household through the dry season, and only part of assessed dams would hold enough water for reported beneficiaries [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. Several literature units are review citations or vote counts, the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements, and the Ethiopian compiler notes that off-site impacts of the recently built check dam still need assessment [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6716_2023_water_availability]. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2]. The check-dam and pond findings are secondary citations in reviews, and the Korean result is modelled in a high-income setting [ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. The Somali haffir compiler itself records improved local water availability with little positive downstream effects [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7777_2026_water_availability]. Groundwater-recharge evidence for these structures now sits in the catchment water yield rows, which also answer what upstream capture does to water downstream.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for gully plugging with check dams in Nepal, stone check walls and check dams in India and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1493_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings with no stated reasoning or measurement, and the Chinese check-dam and Indian farm-pond sheets rate drainage as unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_excess_water_drainage].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for check dams in India and for stone lines, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced, the Somali compiler noting the structures stabilised the landscape and reduced damage from intense rainfall and stormwater runoff [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are compiler ratings with no measurement, and the storm ratings concern rain-storm runoff damage rather than wind [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate jessour in Tunisia and spate irrigation in Eritrea as coping well with drought, and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia as coping moderately [ev_asset_drought_wocat_1013_2011_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1333_2010_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_6715_2023_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings with no observed damage data; spate systems depend on flood flows, so drought is more likely to cut their water supply than to damage the structures.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate jessour in Tunisia and spate irrigation in Eritrea as coping well with local rainstorms, water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia as coping moderately, and marab agriculture in Jordan as coping very well [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1013_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1333_2010_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6715_2023_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5770_2020_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Large floods could wash out traditional spate diversion structures in Yemen, making it hard to get floodwater onto the land, and the WOCAT compiler for jessour in Tunisia rates them as not coping well with river floods [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1013_2011_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Yemen statement refers to diversions before project improvements, and compilers for water spreading in Sudan and spate irrigation in Eritrea rate coping as good, water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia as moderate and marab agriculture in Jordan as very good [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1292_2015_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1333_2010_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6715_2023_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood]. All ratings are practitioner judgements without damage records.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate jessour in Tunisia and spate irrigation in Eritrea as coping well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1013_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1333_2010_local_windstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without observed damage or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The compiler of a WOCAT sheet on water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia judged habitat and plant diversity slightly increased; no mechanism is described.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single technology sheet supplies all units and it rated animal diversity unchanged; these are practitioner judgements, not measurements.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Compilers of WOCAT sheets for marab floodplain water harvesting in Jordan, water spreading in Sudan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate soil organic matter increased under these flood-spreading systems, and the Ethiopian sheet also rates emissions reduced; the sheets give no mechanism for these ratings.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements with no compiler comment, not measurements; the Jordan sheet rates the gain strongly while the Sudan and Ethiopia sheets rate it as slight, and soil organic matter and emission ratings stand in for sequestration.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Yemen, groundwater tables downstream of spate and conservation structures were maintained or increased, and although the main purpose of the spate irrigation systems was to capture floodwater, a large number of the beneficiary farmers interviewed indicated that groundwater levels increased considerably [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_2]. Groundwater is used here as a component of catchment water yield.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units come from one World Bank completion report — a results-framework comment and farmer interviews — so the evidence is self-reported, from one country, with no figure for recharge or flow [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_2]. No unit measures flow below the diversions.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled costs are the up-front investment in floodwater-diversion systems: compiler-reported establishment costs per hectare from WOCAT sheets for Tunisia and Jordan (the Jordan sheet's total spread over 10 ha), and the average investment cost of spate systems under a World Bank project in Yemen, reported at USD 800-1200 per hectare with farmers contributing a 15-20% share.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables for the documented technology, summed and converted to USD with the sheet's own exchange rate; they are not market prices. The cost class rests on the Tunisian sheet alone, because the Yemen completion-report range has no single value and the Jordan sheet is an upper-middle-income case; the Yemen report itself calls the farmer contribution comparatively high, and none of these is a cost per hectare restored.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for a floodplain marab system in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate drought impacts as reduced [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are compiler ratings with no comment or measurement behind them, and the Jordanian sheet is from an upper-middle-income country outside the target band [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_drought_impacts].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Compilers of WOCAT sheets on marab floodplain water harvesting in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia judge drought impacts reduced, without describing the mechanism.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Only practitioner judgements from technology sheets, with no measurement; the Jordan sheet comes from an upper-middle-income context adjacent to the target.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Spate and diversion structures slow and spread flood flows: Bank reporting from Yemen says they reduce soil erosion and control floods while distributing water more evenly to downstream farmers, and WOCAT compilers in Tunisia, Sudan, Jordan and Ethiopia rate downstream flooding as reduced, the Ethiopian compiler noting the structure reduces the speed and volume of downstream flooding [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1013_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1292_2015_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Yemen statement is an assertion in a Bank completion report, and the remaining units are WOCAT compiler ratings; none measures flood peaks or damage [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4]. The Jordanian compiler's comment states reduced flooding is desired rather than observed [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_downstream_flooding].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Jessour, water spreading, marab floodplain systems and water-spreading weirs reduce the speed and volume of downstream flooding, as the Ethiopian weir compiler states, and the Yemen completion report says spate and diversion structures control floods and distribute water more evenly to downstream farmers.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The pool is practitioner judgements from technology sheets in Tunisia, Sudan, Jordan and Ethiopia plus a lender self-reported assertion from Yemen; none measures flood peaks or volumes.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Jessour in Tunisia, water spreading in Sudan, spate irrigation in Eritrea, marab floodplain farming in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia divert and spread floodwater over fields as spate or supplementary irrigation, and compilers rate crop and fodder production as increased [ev_crop_yield_wocat_6715_2023_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1013_2011_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1333_2010_crop_production]. Much of the gain is fed to livestock: crops in the Jordan marab are used as fodder, crop residues in Eritrea feed animals, and Ethiopian compilers link fodder gains to the soil and moisture conserved behind the structure [ev_crop_yield_wocat_5770_2020_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1333_2010_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_6715_2023_fodder_production].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner rating from a WOCAT technology sheet; there is no literature measurement in this cell. The Ethiopian rating is stated as the expert's conviction, and the Sudan rating is relative to nothing being grown otherwise, so the scale of the gain is a counterfactual judgement rather than a yield comparison [ev_crop_yield_wocat_6715_2023_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_1292_2015_crop_production].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The spate family's recurrent cost is the compiler's yearly maintenance table for a Jordanian marab floodplain system, costed over its ten hectares and expressed per hectare per year [ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_maintenance].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: One practitioner-reported figure from an upper-middle-income country, outside the target band; the cost class for the low- and lower-middle-income context cannot rest on it [ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_maintenance].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Compilers of WOCAT sheets for jessour in Tunisia, spate irrigation in Eritrea, water spreading in Sudan, marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan and water spreading weirs in Ethiopia judge these floodwater-diverting systems to have improved food self-sufficiency and increased farm income, and those that rate it judge the risk of production failure to have decreased. The Ethiopian compiler attributes this to improved crop resilience from better soil moisture [ev_food_security_wocat_6715_2023_risk_of_production_failure]. The same compilers rate the long-term returns on establishment and maintenance as positive or very positive.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner judgement from a documented technology sheet, including the benefit-versus-cost ratings, not a household survey or measured income change, and poverty is reached only through food-security and farm-income proxies. Short-term returns on establishment are rated very negative in Tunisia and slightly negative in Jordan, reflecting heavy up-front works, and the Jordanian sheet comes from an upper-middle-income setting.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Spate and water-spreading structures control flood flows on the land: in Yemen spate development reduces damage to wadi banks and lets areas re-green, and Ethiopian compilers say the physical barriers stop soil and water loss [ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_soil_loss]. Sheets for jessour in Tunisia, marab farming in Jordan and water spreading in Sudan rate soil loss, surface runoff or downstream siltation as reduced [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1013_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1292_2015_surface_runoff].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The only literature unit is a farmer-perception figure in a lender completion report from Yemen [ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5]; the rest are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets, and the Jordan siltation comment states a desired rather than observed outcome [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5770_2020_downstream_siltation]. Runoff reduction and sediment retention enter as component proxies.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sheets for jessour in Tunisia, marab floodplain farming in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate downstream siltation as reduced, as floodwater and its sediment are spread and held on the fields [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1013_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5770_2020_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings of downstream siltation, a component proxy for water quality, and the Jordan comment states reduced siltation as a desired rather than an observed outcome [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5770_2020_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Spate and water-spreading systems divert floodwater onto fields: WOCAT compilers for jessour in Tunisia, spate irrigation in Eritrea, water spreading in Sudan, marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan and water spreading weirs in Ethiopia judge them to improve water harvesting, and the Ethiopian compiler credits the weirs with a positive contribution to groundwater in adjacent farms [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6715_2023_water_availability].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The WOCAT units are practitioner judgements rather than measurements. The Sudan compiler judges no change in water availability [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability], and the Ethiopian compiler notes the weirs are too recent to judge off-site impacts [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6715_2023_water_availability]. The Yemeni groundwater reports now sit in the spate catchment water yield row.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without stated reasoning or measurement, from technologies built to spread floodwater over fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_excess_water_drainage].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The only unit is the WOCAT compiler rating for water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia, which records no change in the impacts of cyclones and rain storms, so no mechanism is evidenced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single compiler rating from one technology sheet, with no comment or measurement, neither supports nor rules out an effect [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate terraces, stone lines and stone bunds in China, Rwanda, Yemen, Cabo Verde, Uganda, Niger, Haiti and Tunisia as coping well with drought, and bench terraces in Bangladesh as coping moderately [ev_asset_drought_wocat_1522_2010_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1553_2012_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_6610_2022_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_4284_2018_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings of coping, with no observed damage or failure data.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau, with few local funds to repair it, poorly structured vineyard terraces in Spain suffered severe landslides after a single rainstorm, and in Algeria a poorly maintained banquette network fails in a chain reaction during torrential and prolonged rains, the smallest unrepaired breach spreading sliding through the whole network [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av]. WOCAT compilers judge radical terraces in Rwanda, stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde and contour stone bunds in Niger not to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7, ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1616_2014_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Other compilers judge progressive bench terraces in China, stone-covered bench terraces in Yemen, stone lines in Uganda, vetiver-hedge terraces in Haiti and bench terraces in Bangladesh to cope well with rainstorms, and a continuous bench terrace for tea in Thailand to cope very well [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1522_2010_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1560_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1589_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_3223_2017_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4281_2018_local_rainstorm]; thunderstorms are rated as coping moderately for Bangladesh terraces and vegetated stone bunds in Burkina Faso, while Bangladesh terraces cope very well with hailstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6729_2023_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_local_hailstorm]. Damage in the literature follows poor construction or maintenance (poorly structured terraces in Spain, poorly maintained banquettes in Algeria) and the Loess Plateau evaluation gives no measure of damage, so the rest of the evidence is compiler ratings [ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av, ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av, ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for bench terraces in Bangladesh rates them as coping moderately with forest fire and well with land fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_forest_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_land_fire].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units come from one technology sheet and are practitioner ratings without observed damage.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Banquettes lack the capacity to absorb runoff from erosive rains and overflow, diversion channels fill with eroded soil and overflow in the heaviest storms, and torrential rain collapses terrace walls or carries small terraces away in mass movements [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5].
