WOCAT compilers judge radical terraces in Rwanda and contour stone bunds in Niger not to cope well with river floods, while stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde, stone lines in Tunisia and gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan are judged to cope well [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1553_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1616_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1573_2013_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6610_2022_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7553_2025_flash_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Failure is tied to maintenance and setting: rarely maintained diversion systems generally fail after 4 to 10 years, terrace collapse is linked to abandonment, and the Rwandan mass movement happened on terraces without trees [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. The literature hazards are erosive rains, torrential rain and mass movements mapped to flood and come as expert and modelled statements without failure rates, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets rather than records of damage [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Slope failure damages terraces where slopes are unstable or terraces are abandoned: in the Tizi Ouzou region of Algeria 19% of banquettes on marls and clays were damaged by landslides and as many by gullying, and in Mediterranean regions over 50% of abandoned terraces were vulnerable to gully erosion and landslides that collapse the dry-stone walls [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: WOCAT compilers judge stone lines in Tunisia and a continuous bench terrace for tea in a high sloping area of Thailand to cope well with landslides, and vetiver-hedge bench terraces with trees in Haiti and bench terraces on hilly slopes in Bangladesh to cope very well [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6610_2022_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4281_2018_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_3223_2017_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4284_2018_landslide]. The damage figures are secondary citations tied to marl and clay substrates and to abandonment rather than to maintained terraces, and the ratings are practitioner judgements [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde and contour stone bunds in Niger as coping well with local windstorms, vetiver bench terraces in Haiti as coping well with tropical storms, and bench terraces in Bangladesh as coping moderately with both [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1573_2013_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1616_2014_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_3223_2017_tropical_storm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4284_2018_tropical_storm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage, and the progressive bench terrace in China is rated as not coping well with local windstorms, with no reason given [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1522_2010_local_windstorm].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for contour stone bunds in Bhutan links higher plant diversity to the soil becoming suitable for more diverse crops, and the compiler for bench terraces in Bangladesh expects soil flora and fauna to find a suitable environment once the planned cropping system is established [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4284_2018_animal_diversity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are compiler ratings from technology sheets, not measurements; the Bhutan rating describes crop diversity and the Bangladesh rating an anticipated rather than observed change, so neither speaks to wild species.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terracing and stone lines are rated by their compilers as building below-ground soil organic matter on treated land, through an expanding root system under orchard terraces and retained soil behind stone lines [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7553_2025_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1589_2013_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_6610_2022_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C]; one bench-terrace sheet also rates emissions as reduced because the crops of a more intensive rotation absorb carbon [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_4284_2018_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. The same preprint meta-analysis finds terracing raised soil organic carbon by 27%, 17.94% and 26.62% in three Chinese regions, with increases of 14.11% to 60.96% in regional subsets 11 to 30 years after construction [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_5, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_6, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_7, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_9, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_11].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner rating from a technology sheet, not a measured carbon stock; the stone-bund sheet says organic matter falls at the top of the terrace and rises at the bottom, a redistribution within the field rather than a net gain [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_6891_2023_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C], and the bench-terrace rationale is higher cropping intensity, which is not long-term storage [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_4284_2018_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C]. The preprint now sets the strength of this row: it has not been peer reviewed, it is from an upper-middle-income country, and its duration figures are the windows with obvious increases, overlapping the regional estimates [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and contour ridges retain rainfall on slopes so part of it recharges groundwater: in Cameroon terraces would cause a groundwater recharge of 15 to 25% of rainfall, with drainage through rock fissures that could reach the piedmonts [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1], and hydrological modelling of contour ridges in Morocco, structures that promote the slow formation of terraces by sediment accumulation, estimates a 50% increase in recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1]. Recharge is used here as a component of catchment water yield.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Recharge stands in for catchment yield; no unit measures flow leaving the catchment. The Cameroonian figure is a conditional estimate and the Moroccan figure a modelling result, both cited secondarily [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1]. The Cameroonian source flags that the drainage could reach the unterraced piedmonts, a much more fragile environment [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1]. On-slope supply evidence for terraces is in the terracing water stress row.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled costs are establishment costs per hectare for terraces and bunds: compiler-reported WOCAT sheet costs for Ethiopia, Yemen, Uganda, Uzbekistan (a total spread over 1.6 ha) and Cabo Verde, plus the cost of rehabilitating pre-Columbian terraces (andenes) in Peru, a heavy earth- and stone-moving intervention. A review also tabulates terracing costs from China of 1918 to 4045 USD per hectare (mechanisation, labour and socioeconomic costs), rising with the original slope from 5 to 25 degrees [ev_project_cost_wei16_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables for the documented technology, summed and converted to USD with the sheet's own exchange rate; they are not market prices. Converted values span from under a dollar to tens of thousands of USD per hectare, so the Uganda and Yemen sheets look like entry or conversion problems rather than real costs; the Peru figure is a 1994 rehabilitation cost cited secondhand, and the Peru and Cabo Verde units come from upper-middle-income settings. The Chinese terracing costs are a secondary table from an upper-middle-income setting and rise with slope [ev_project_cost_wei16_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: When rainfall is erratic, stone bunds conserve more moisture in the soil and ease crop water stress during dry spells, and crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. Rwandan land-husbandry project households showed greater resilience than controls to the 2016 drought and recovered faster, and WOCAT compilers for terraces and stone lines in Haiti, Bangladesh, Tunisia and Uzbekistan rate drought impacts as reduced, the Uzbek compiler noting that more water is captured and infiltrated [ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_4284_2018_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield benefit in the driest year (1985) and so did not reduce famine risk then, which bounds the cited dry-year gain [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. The Rwandan finding comes from a bundled package whose terrace share is unknown, most other units are WOCAT compiler ratings, and the Haiti compiler states the impact has not yet been measured [ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_drought_impacts].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and stone lines capture and infiltrate more water so the land is less susceptible to drought, as the compiler for gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan puts it; compilers for terraces in Haiti and Bangladesh and stone lines in Tunisia also judge drought impacts reduced, and households in a Rwandan land husbandry and water harvesting project proved more resilient than controls to the 2016 drought and recovered faster.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The WOCAT units are practitioner judgements, and the Haiti compiler notes the impact has not yet been measured; the Rwanda result is an impact evaluation against controls reported second-hand in a completion report, without a magnitude or outcome metric.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The only unit is the compiler-reported establishment cost of a 200 m vetiver line in Haiti, from a single WOCAT technology sheet's cost table converted to USD with the sheet's exchange rate.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: One compiler-reported figure for one structure type, not a market price or a measured project cost; a vetiver hedge line is a light, vegetative structure and is not representative of stone or earth terrace construction.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: On intensively tended terraces all crop residues are grazed off as soon as harvests end, so bush fires have little fuel, and the WOCAT compiler for bench terraces in Bangladesh rates fire risk as reduced [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_4284_2018_fire_risk].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The terrace statement is an expert estimate its authors say has no experimental basis on terraces, and the Bangladesh unit is a practitioner rating with no stated reasoning [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_4284_2018_fire_risk]. The effect depends on residues being removed by grazing.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and contour stone bunds slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces lowered mean runoff and flood peaks on small mountain plots, stone bunds lower hillslope peak discharges and in high-rainfall years protect land from rapid flow in heavy rain, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment reduced flood runoff volume, clipped peaks and lengthened flood duration [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_2, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s]. Compacted hill terraces with retention walls in Uttarakhand, India are credited with mitigating flood and landslide impact, and WOCAT compilers for terraces and stone lines in Rwanda, China, Tunisia, Uzbekistan and other countries rate flooding as reduced, the Tunisian compiler noting stone lines and walls reduce peak flows during heavy rainfall [ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1553_2012_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1522_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Diversion banquettes and ditches, filed in this family, do the opposite: in Niger they raised peak discharges, and runoff-diversion systems accelerate concentration time with serious gullying risk if the dikes break [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. Catchment-level peak-flow evidence for terraces is scarce, the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, the Uttarakhand claim is a Bank self-report, and most units are WOCAT compiler ratings [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, stone lines and contour stone bunds detain and spread runoff on slopes, lowering peak discharges and making flows last longer after rain; in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment a combined treatment cut the runoff volume of 71 single-peak floods by 50%, and WOCAT compilers for terraces and stone lines in many countries judge downstream flooding reduced, the Tunisian stone-lines sheet citing lower peak flows during heavy rainfall.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Diversion banquettes in Niger and runoff-diversion dikes raised peak discharges, and breached dikes risk gullying, so design decides the sign. Catchment-scale evidence is scarce, with a review calling the terrace effect on peak flow uncertain; the Tunisian treatment also included rangeland closure, the Uttarakhand flood-mitigation claim is lender self-reported, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements rather than measurements.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces, fanya juu and contour stone bunds or lines level slopes and slow runoff so more water and soil stay on the field; yields of maize, barley, millet and sorghum rose on terraced or bunded land, especially in dry years. Stone bunds raised sorghum yields by 33% to 55% in Burkina Faso and by about 142% with compost, and millet yields in Niger rose by more than 40% up to 15 years after the bunds were built [ev_crop_yield_zoug14_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. WOCAT compilers add that stone lines in Tunisia protect farmland from degradation, contour stone bunds in Bhutan enlarge the cultivable area as stones are removed, and Gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan turn unproductive land productive [ev_crop_yield_wocat_6610_2022_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_6891_2023_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_7553_2025_crop_production]. Meta-analyses support the gain: a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds a 48% yield increase for terraces, an Ethiopian synthesis a mean gain of 322 kg per hectare for stone bunds with soil total nitrogen up from 0.16 to 0.20%, and a terracing meta-analysis finds biomass on terraces about 1.94 times that on slopes, and reviewed studies report terraced teff, barley and maize yields at least two times those on slopes and 20% gains on young bench terraces in Peru [ev_crop_yield_wei16_1, ev_crop_yield_wei16_2, ev_crop_yield_wei16_4]; reviewed studies also report maize yields up nearly 50% on fanya juu terraces in semi-arid Kenya, wheat yields 6–7 times higher on stone-wall terraces than on slopes under the same input costs, and land productivity over 19% higher on bench terraces [ev_crop_yield_tefe24_5, ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_soil_nitrogen_adim16_1, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_4, ev_crop_yield_wei16_3, ev_agricultural_production_value_wei16_1]. In Burkina Faso, crop yields in years of average rainfall rose by 63–74 per cent on farms using rock bunds [ev_crop_yield_sawa11h1_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Several literature figures are lender self-reports (Rwanda before/after yields, Indian with/without models bundled with crop packages); the Rwanda value-of-harvest gain is from an independent DIME evaluation, and the Burkina Faso and Niger gains are cited from earlier studies, the largest bundled with compost [ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7, ev_crop_yield_utk22_8, ev_agricultural_production_value_rwa18_3, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4]. Diversion banquettes in Niger reduced yields, progressive terraces on poor soils in Rwanda gave no yield increase, bench terraces need heavy fertility restoration before yields rise, and a Haitian compiler notes that on very degraded land farmers must wait for the soil to recover [ev_crop_yield_heusch95_1, ev_crop_yield_roose06_3, ev_crop_yield_roose94_4, ev_crop_yield_wocat_3223_2017_crop_production]. Most pooled units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets rather than measurements. Stone bunds in semi-arid Tanzania reduced maize yield by 13% [ev_crop_yield_adim16_9], and in Algeria farmers lost 5 to 15% of their cropped area to banquettes without seeing yields improve, legume yields between banquettes showed no significant gain, and a Moroccan farmer saw no yield improvement between banquettes imposed by technicians [ev_crop_yield_arab04_1, ev_crop_yield_arab04_2, ev_crop_yield_roos10_2]. The terracing meta-analysis pools unweighted ratios and several of the largest multiples are single studies cited in reviews [ev_crop_yield_wei16_1, ev_crop_yield_wei16_3]. The Burkina Faso rock-bund gain is for years the authors call average rainfall, with compost on the bunded fields [ev_crop_yield_sawa11h1_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled costs are compiler-reported annual maintenance costs from WOCAT sheets for terraces and bunds, per hectare in Ethiopia, Yemen and Uganda and per structure for a 200 m vetiver line in Haiti.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables for the documented technology, summed and converted to USD with the sheet's own exchange rate; they are not market prices. The per-hectare values run from a few cents in Uganda to a few hundred USD in Yemen, so the Uganda figure looks like an entry or conversion problem, and the Haiti sheet's annual maintenance per line exceeds its own establishment cost.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terracing raises yields and enables higher-value crops on former hillsides, which drives positive modelled returns per hectare and improved food consumption in project households; terrace investments are judged to pay off over long lifetimes, mainly where they carry high-value crops such as vegetables [ev_economic_return_rwa18_8, ev_food_security_rwa18_5, ev_economic_return_willem21_1, ev_economic_return_fao13c_1]. WOCAT compilers report continuous income from tea on bench terraces in Thailand, a per-hectare income gain from progressive bench terraces in China, contour stone bunds in Bhutan meeting household maize demand, and Gradoni terraces in Uzbekistan improving drought resilience [ev_household_income_wocat_4281_2018_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1522_2010_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_6891_2023_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_7553_2025_risk_of_production_failure]. Compilers' benefit-versus-cost ratings are mostly positive or very positive over the long term. An Ethiopian synthesis reports positive net present values of 3486.2 Birr per hectare for stone bunds, 2794.0 for bench terraces and 5283.4 for level fanya juu [ev_economic_return_adim16_1, ev_economic_return_adim16_2, ev_economic_return_adim16_3], and modelled bench-terrace gains in Peru could raise per capita incomes by up to 15% [ev_household_income_wei16_1]. A review cites soil and water conservation measures, including level bunds and fanya juu terraces, boosting farmer income by increasing soil fertility, yield and water [ev_household_income_tade23h1_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets; the literature returns are lender crop-budget models for Rwanda and India, and the food-security gain is an independent DIME evaluation [ev_economic_return_rwa18_8, ev_household_income_utk22_9, ev_food_security_rwa18_5]. A review reports terraces reducing net crop income in Ethiopia and banquette profitability in Niger was close to nil; compilers record no change in food security for vetiver terraces in Haiti, where farmers must wait for degraded soil to recover, and on sheets from Rwanda [ev_household_income_mala24_1, ev_economic_return_heusch95_1, ev_food_security_wocat_3223_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Food security, income and returns are proxies for poverty. Compilers rate short-term returns on establishment as slightly negative to negative on sheets from Rwanda, Yemen, Cabo Verde and Uzbekistan, and Rwanda's short-term maintenance return as very negative; these are practitioner judgements, not measured returns. The Ethiopian net present values are unweighted means from a few studies each, and the Peruvian income gain is a modelled potential cited in a review [ev_economic_return_adim16_2, ev_household_income_wei16_1]. The Ethiopian income claim is cited from a study that the citing review itself describes as methodologically weak [ev_household_income_tade23h1_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, contour stone bunds and lines and banquettes shorten slope length and slow runoff, so soil losses on steep plots fall sharply and sediment loads drop where terracing is widespread. Terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots on 20 to 60% slopes from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, a contour banquette in Niger divided erosion by 150 against traditional cropping, and stone bunds with compost cut total soil loss by 79% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_1]. WOCAT compilers rate soil loss and runoff as reduced on terraces from China to Uzbekistan, noting that stone lines in Tunisia cut runoff by 50% and that Gradoni terraces trap soil eroded from the inter-spaces [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_6610_2022_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1522_2010_surface_runoff]. Meta-analyses agree: a terracing meta-analysis finds erosion control on terraces 11.46 times that of controls and runoff reduction 2.6 times [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_1], a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds terraces cut soil loss by 60.21% and runoff by 56.5%, and an Ethiopian synthesis reports stone bunds cutting soil loss by 38% and runoff by 34.4% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_5, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_3, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_3, ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_3]. Reviews also report terracing reducing runoff by 92.6% and 80% in sub-humid and humid regions, stone lines and terraces reducing runoff and erosion by 30 to 50%, sediment accumulating behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, and fanya juu trapping 64% of sediment, rising to 80% with vetiver grass [ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_2, ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_3, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Alignment decides the sign: diversion banquettes in Niger doubled runoff coefficients and increased gully erosion, while contour banquettes in the same region cut erosion; ditches with downslope banks cause rill erosion, many Maghreb banquettes were erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. The Rwanda sediment reductions are lender-monitored before/after figures without a control, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements rather than measurements [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_2]. Bench terracing alone reduced runoff by only 9% in a small USA watershed, gullied area on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, poorly maintained Algerian banquettes accelerate erosion, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on downstream dam sedimentation [ev_runoff_reduction_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. The meta-analytic ratios are unweighted, and the Ethiopian stone-bund sediment figure comes with a total soil loss of 77 t per hectare, so bunds trap most but not all eroded soil [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terracing and retaining walls hold soil on slopes, which an evaluation in Morocco expects to reduce siltation of downstream rivers and dam storage [ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. WOCAT compilers rate downstream siltation as reduced for radical terraces in Rwanda, bench terraces in Yemen and Bangladesh, stone lines in Uganda and Tunisia, contour stone bunds in Niger and vetiver terraces in Haiti [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1553_2012_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1560_2013_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1616_2014_downstream_siltation]. Reviews add that sediment accumulates behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, fanya juu trapped 64% of sediment (80% with vetiver grass), and bench terracing cut sediment yield by 58% in a small USA watershed [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Morocco unit is an evaluator assertion and the rest are practitioner ratings; nothing on water chemistry is measured, and siltation is a component proxy [ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. The Gradoni terrace sheet for Uzbekistan rates only a slight reduction [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_7553_2025_downstream_siltation]. The added sediment figures are secondary citations in a review, the bench-terrace figure comes from a high-income watershed, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of a downstream dam over 1947-1968 [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and stone lines capture and retain rainwater on slopes, and stone lines contribute to increased infiltration of rainwater into the soil, thereby replenishing water resources [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_availability]. WOCAT compilers judge bench terraces in Yemen, stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde, contour stone bunds in Niger and gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan to improve water harvesting, and radical terraces in Rwanda, vetiver terraces in Haiti, stone lines in Tunisia and semi-circular stone bunds in Ethiopia to improve water quantity or availability [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1560_2013_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_availability].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The WOCAT units are practitioner judgements, and catchment modelling in Peru found no difference in crop water distribution with partial terracing [ev_water_regulation_willem21_1]. Abandoned or degraded terraces worsen water regulation [ev_water_regulation_willem21_2]. The recharge estimates for terraces and contour ridges now sit in the terracing catchment water yield row.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Stone bunds hold runoff in the field, and in wet years this can waterlog parts of the field and harm crop production; millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3]. WOCAT compilers for terraces in Peru, Yemen and Cabo Verde instead rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1560_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The harm comes from cited statements from Burkina Faso that apply only to wet years or very wet months and give no magnitude, while the opposing units are practitioner ratings for bench and stone-wall terraces rather than stone bunds, so the two sides may describe different structures [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for radical terraces in Rwanda, vetiver bench terraces in Haiti and stone lines in Tunisia rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_1553_2012_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings concerning rain-storm damage rather than wind, and the Haiti compiler says the impact is not yet measured [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: Check dams, gabions, fascines, terraces and bunds trap sediment that would otherwise reach streams, canals and reservoirs, lowering catchment sediment export and downstream siltation [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. WOCAT compilers describe gabion walls and check dams in Somalia trapping sediment upstream and reducing siltation of downstream fields and water bodies, and vegetative check dams in Madagascar reducing siltation of downstream rice fields [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6478_2022_downstream_siltation]. Measured retention now spans scales: check dams on China's Loess Plateau are credited with cutting regional sediment export by about 85% and accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction at the outlets of five catchments over 26 years, and loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of watershed sediment yield [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1]; sediment accumulates behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, fanya juu trapped 64% of sediment (80% with vetiver grass), and bench terracing cut sediment yield by 58% in a small USA watershed [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5]; and small ponds trapped 54-85% of incoming sediment over 8 years in southern Germany and 68% over the long term in Belgium [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. Holding soil also holds nutrients: an Ethiopian synthesis finds graded soil bunds reduced total nitrogen lost in runoff and sediment by up to 48% [ev_nutrient_removal_adim16_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: The class follows the sub-practice vote, not the pooled result. The in-field row holds the strongest result, strong positive, but it rests on WOCAT ratings for pits, stone lines and contour bunds in Niger and conservation tillage in Kenya and Zambia, plus the Ethiopian graded-bund nitrogen synthesis [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1100_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1219_2014_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1652_2014_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_940_2010_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_siltation, ev_nutrient_removal_adim16_1]. The rows that carry the measured trapping studies — check dams and ponds (runoff catchment) and terraces and bunds (terracing) — hold moderate positive, as do the micro-catchment and spate rows; the cross-family row, a single modelled Chinese programme figure, holds slight positive [ev_sediment_retention_iegchn07_5]. The weighted median is moderate positive, below the pooled strong. Water quality is inferred almost entirely from sediment retention, a component proxy, plus nutrient losses in runoff from a single synthesis; nothing on water chemistry downstream is measured, and many units are practitioner ratings of downstream siltation from WOCAT sheets. Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of a downstream dam over 1947-1968, and the twofold decline in outlet sediment yield with USA check dams was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Much of the literature is secondary citations in reviews, several from high-income settings (USA, Germany, Belgium), the China programme figure is modelled, and gabions in Morocco have filled and need raising [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_iegchn07_5, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1]. A sheet from Niger rates siltation unchanged, the Zambian tillage sheet expects a benefit only at large scale, and the Ethiopian compiler notes the trapped sediment has not been quantified [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1614_2014_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: In semi-arid catchments check dams on China's Loess Plateau are credited with cutting regional sediment export by about 85% and accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction at the outlets of five catchments over 26 years, and loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of watershed sediment yield [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: The USA check dams halved outlet sediment per unit of peak runoff, but this was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Sediment retention is a component proxy for water quality, the Chinese figures are secondary citations in reviews, and the USA site is high-income rangeland rather than smallholder farmland [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: In high-income settings loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of watershed sediment yield, small ponds trapped 54-85% of incoming sediment over 8 years in southern Germany and 68% over the long term in Belgium, and bench terracing cut sediment yield by 58% in a small USA watershed [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: The halving of outlet sediment by the USA check dams was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Sediment retention is a component proxy for water quality, most figures are secondary citations in a review, and rangeland and arable-field ponds in high-income countries transfer only loosely to smallholder water harvesting [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings check dams on China's Loess Plateau are credited with cutting regional sediment export by about 85% and accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction at the outlets of five catchments over 26 years, and WOCAT compilers for works in Peru, Thailand and Jordan rate downstream siltation as reduced [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1506_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_4281_2018_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5770_2020_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5860_2021_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam over 1947-1968 [ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. The Chinese figures are secondary citations, the Jordanian compiler comments only that reduced siltation is desired, and the ratings are practitioner judgements; sediment retention is a component proxy for water quality [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5770_2020_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Bunds, stone lines, micro-basins and check dams capture and retain rainwater so that it infiltrates, and compilers and local people report raised well levels; sand dams and subsurface dams store water that extends the months of water access or backs up wells when other sources dry up, production cisterns keep livestock watered, and participating villages in India reduced water transport by tanker. WOCAT compilers for jessour, spate and water-spreading systems, bunds, terraces, check dams, sand dams, ponds and haffirs from Tunisia, Niger, Ethiopia, Kenya, India, Somalia and elsewhere judge them to improve water harvesting, water quantity or water availability. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1]. A check-dam review reports that check dams storing seasonal runoff solve local supply scarcity; traditional rainwater ponds in South Korea reduced the occurrence of water deficit from 30 to 20% [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. In India, discharge of springs and streams rose in treated watersheds: a sample study in Himachal Pradesh reports a 40 percent increase in water discharge in spring and stream sources [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1], and the Uttarakhand project achieved an average 21 percent increase in water discharge from perennial water sources in sampled micro-watersheds, against a target of 25 percent [ev_water_regulation_utk22_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Most literature units are narrative, perception or lender-reported, the pooled percentages mix spring-discharge, water-deficit and tanker-use metrics, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets rather than measurements; compilers judge no change in water availability for water spreading in Sudan and semi-circular bunds in Niger, and Ethiopian compilers note that off-site effects of recently built structures are yet to be assessed [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1614_2014_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6715_2023_water_availability]. Groundwater-recharge evidence, with its limits, now sits in the catchment water yield rows. Many sand dams cannot supply a household through the dry season [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3]. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2]. The check-dam and pond findings are secondary citations in reviews, and the Korean result is modelled in a high-income setting [ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. The Indian spring and stream discharge figures come from World Bank completion reports, the lender's own evaluation, measured before and after without untreated comparison sites, for catchment treatment that bundles plantations, trenches, ponds and check dams with water-harvesting structures, so the gain cannot be credited to water harvesting alone [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1, ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. What upstream capture does to water downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Storage and recharge structures ease water stress in semi-arid areas: production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil keep livestock watered while clay tanks are dry, an agency review credits consumption and production cisterns with a large drop in rural establishments without any water source, and subsurface dams raise water levels in existing wells used when other sources dry up [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Supply is bounded by storage: 57% of Kenyan sand dams would hold 4 months of water for their reported beneficiaries [ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. The Brazilian units are implementer or agency assessments, interviews or census inference from an upper-middle-income context rather than the low-income target [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5]. Well-level evidence for semi-arid bunds and zaï now sits in the catchment water yield rows. What upstream capture does to water downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: In low and lower-middle-income settings, pits, bunds, terraces and check dams increase infiltration and groundwater recharge, raising well levels and spring discharge, and sand dams store water that extends the months of water access. WOCAT compilers for jessour, spate and water-spreading systems, bunds, terraces, check dams, sand dams, ponds and haffirs from Tunisia, Niger, Ethiopia, Kenya, India, Somalia and elsewhere judge them to improve water harvesting, water quantity or water availability.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Many literature units are lender-reported or community perceptions and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets; compilers judge no change in water availability for water spreading in Sudan and semi-circular bunds in Niger [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1614_2014_water_availability]. Groundwater gains in India could be wiped out by increased pumping, year-round wells did not increase in Burkina Faso, and many Kenyan sand dams lack capacity to supply even one household through the dry season [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2, ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: In semi-arid Brazil, domestic and production cisterns and subsurface dams store rain for the dry season, giving households basic drinking water, keeping livestock watered and reducing dependence on water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1]. A few catchment studies of trenches observe reduced quick runoff or increased aquifer recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Storage limits the benefit: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, larger households stay dependent on water trucks, and only 19.1% of surveyed families used the cistern as their main source [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2]. Catchment effects are weak or unproven: recharge gains cannot be generalised, trenches have little effect on baseflow and no significant effect on infiltration rates, terracing 20% of cropland made no difference in a Peruvian catchment model, and abandoned terraces can harm water regulation [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1, ev_water_regulation_locat20_1, ev_soil_permeability_locat20_1, ev_water_regulation_willem21_1, ev_water_regulation_willem21_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: The evidence splits by sub-practice, and the separator is where the water is held. Practices that hold water on the cropped field — the in-field family (pits, planting basins, mulch, conservation tillage) and the stone bunds in the terracing family — can backfire in wet conditions: stone bunds can waterlog parts of the field in wet years, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the humid Sudanian zone of Cameroon, where rainfall exceeds 1 200 mm per year, sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. A conservation agriculture meta-analysis adds that 92% of the data show mulch cover in high-rainfall areas lowering maize yields through waterlogging [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3], and in an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, waterlogging lasting 3–5 days during early maize growth also affected the mulching and basin treatments, whose waterlogged plants had yellow leaves and stunted growth [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. WOCAT compilers for pits and stone lines in Niger and conservation tillage in Kenya and the Philippines also rate drainage of excess water as worse [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1100_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_940_2010_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_excess_water_drainage]. Practices that collect or spread runoff in structures point the other way: compilers for check dams in Nepal, India and Ethiopia (runoff catchment) and for water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia and marab floodplain farming in Jordan (spate) rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1493_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage], while the Chinese check-dam and Indian farm-pond sheets rate it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_excess_water_drainage]. Primary sources from southern Africa make the same point: an FAO study shows by a water-balance calculation that planting basins can depress yields when too much water concentrates in them under high rainfall or in seasons with abnormally high rainfall, citing extension reports and farmer testimony of farmers scooping water from the basins [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8], and concludes that in sub-humid environments yields could be affected by water-logging in years with adequate rainfall [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7]. In a Kenyan on-farm trial, ridged plots with fertiliser at the relatively wetter sub-humid Rachuonyo site gave the lowest yields, slightly below conventional practice, which the authors say can probably be explained by waterlogging caused by ridging [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: The roll-up states conflicting evidence because the sub-practice rows disagree in sign and the minority side carries enough of the weight to count: the in-field and terracing rows are negative (the practice worsens waterlogging), the runoff-catchment and spate rows are positive. Neither the pooled negative nor a positive class would describe the practice as a whole; which one applies depends on the sub-practice and on the rainfall regime. The split is also one of evidence type. Every unit on the improving side is a WOCAT practitioner rating with no measured drainage, and the negative rows are not uniform either: terrace sheets in Peru, Yemen and Cabo Verde, a ripper-tillage sheet in Zambia and a composting-pit sheet in Burkina Faso rate drainage improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1560_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1139_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_959_2010_excess_water_drainage]. The harm comes from the literature units, which are tied to wet years or high-rainfall zones and give no magnitude or share of field affected [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1]. The Cameroon zaï and Burkina Faso millet losses come from using the practice outside its rainfall window; under the standing ruling they are held out of the production classes as performance caveats, but this waterlogging hazard cell is where that evidence belongs, and it is counted here [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3]. The Burkina Faso statements are cited rather than measured, and the Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors [ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. The meta-analysis figure is a share of observations, not an effect size [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3]. The Ethiopian waterlogging finding is a field observation with no measured yield loss, and the source names a tillage treatment as the one particularly affected, so only part of the harm can be put on mulch and basins [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. The southern African basin finding rests on a theoretical water balance plus extension reports and farmer testimony, and the author notes there are currently few published data to substantiate it [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8]; the sub-humid conclusion goes beyond what the crop model simulates and covers conservation agriculture as basins or ripping with residue retention, so it is bundled with reduced tillage; neither gives a magnitude [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7]. The Kenyan ridging loss is the authors' probable explanation rather than a measured waterlogging contrast, and the ridging is bundled with fertiliser; because it comes from using the practice at a wetter site than it suits, it is held out of the production classes as an envelope misfit (a suitability caveat) and counted here as waterlogging evidence [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: In low and lower-middle-income settings, stone bunds can waterlog parts of the field in wet years, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and sorghum in zaï pits in the humid Sudanian zone of Cameroon yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields; WOCAT compilers for pits and stone lines in Niger and conservation tillage in Kenya also rate drainage of excess water as worse [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1100_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_940_2010_excess_water_drainage]. Compilers for check dams in Nepal and India, bench terraces in Yemen, water-spreading weirs and check dams in Ethiopia, ripper tillage in Zambia and composted planting pits in Burkina Faso rate drainage as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1493_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_959_2010_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: Harm appears in wet years or high-rainfall zones and is not quantified, and the units that report it are cited statements or an unpublished observation, while the opposing units are practitioner ratings; the Indian farm-pond sheet rates drainage as unchanged [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_excess_water_drainage]. The direction depends on whether a practice ponds water in the field or channels it away.

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for the rehabilitation of ancient terraces in Peru, reinforced stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde and marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings with no measurement; the Philippine conservation-tillage sheet rates drainage as worse and the Chinese check-dam sheet rates it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: Under rainfed cropping the harm comes where water is held on the cropped field in wet conditions: in wet years stone bunds in Burkina Faso may cause waterlogging in some parts of the field, millet production can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the Sudanian zone of Cameroon, where rainfall exceeds 80 mm per day and 1 200 mm per year, sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields because of frequent soil waterlogging and the risk of nutrient leaching [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. A conservation agriculture meta-analysis finds that 92% of the data show mulch cover in high-rainfall areas lowering yields through waterlogging [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3]. WOCAT compilers for pits and stone lines in Niger and conservation tillage in Kenya and the Philippines rate drainage of excess water as worse [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1100_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_940_2010_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_excess_water_drainage]. Primary sources from southern Africa make the same point: an FAO study shows by a water-balance calculation that planting basins can depress yields when too much water concentrates in them under high rainfall or in seasons with abnormally high rainfall, citing extension reports and farmer testimony of farmers scooping water from the basins [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8], and concludes that in sub-humid environments yields could be affected by water-logging in years with adequate rainfall [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: The minority side points the other way, and it is all practitioner ratings: compilers for check dams in Nepal, India and Ethiopia, water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia, marab floodplain farming in Jordan, terraces in Peru, Yemen and Cabo Verde, ripper tillage in Zambia and composted planting pits in Burkina Faso rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1493_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1560_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1139_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_959_2010_excess_water_drainage], while the Chinese check-dam and Indian farm-pond sheets rate it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_excess_water_drainage]. The separator is where the water is held: practices that keep water on the cropped field (pits, mulch, conservation tillage, stone bunds) carry the harm, while structures that collect, spread or terrace runoff are rated as improving drainage. None of the harm sources gives a magnitude or the share of a field affected. The Cameroon zaï, Burkina Faso millet and mulch-cover losses come from using the practice outside its rainfall window; under the standing ruling they are held out of the production classes as performance caveats, and are counted here as waterlogging hazard evidence [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3]. The Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors, the Burkina Faso statements are cited from earlier studies, and the meta-analysis figure is a share of observations, not an effect size [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3]. The southern African basin finding rests on a theoretical water balance plus extension reports and farmer testimony, and the author notes there are currently few published data to substantiate it [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8]; the sub-humid conclusion goes beyond what the crop model simulates and covers conservation agriculture as basins or ripping with residue retention, so it is bundled with reduced tillage; neither gives a magnitude [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: In upper-middle-income countries the only evidence is WOCAT compiler ratings, and most say the practice improves drainage of excess water: compilers for terraces in Peru and Cabo Verde and for marab floodplain farming in Jordan rate drainage as improved, the Peruvian sheet at the top of the scale [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: The ratings split by sub-practice: the Philippine conservation-tillage sheet rates drainage worse and the Chinese check-dam sheet rates it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage], so the improvement belongs to structures that terrace or spread runoff, not to tillage that holds water in the field. No unit is measured; these are compiler judgements without a magnitude, and none covers severe or extreme waterlogging. The measured and cited harm results under rainfed cropping come from low and lower-middle income countries and are outside this scope.

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: Practices that hold water in the field can backfire in wet conditions: stone bunds can waterlog parts of the field in wet years, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the humid Sudanian zone of Cameroon sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. WOCAT compilers for pits and stone lines in Niger, conservation tillage in Kenya and the Philippines also rate drainage of excess water as worse, while compilers for terraces, check dams, water-spreading weirs and other works in Peru, Nepal, India, Yemen, Ethiopia, Cabo Verde and Jordan rate it as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1100_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_940_2010_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1493_2011_excess_water_drainage]. A conservation agriculture meta-analysis adds that 92% of the data show mulch cover in high-rainfall areas lowering maize yields through waterlogging [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, waterlogging lasting 3–5 days during early maize growth also affected the mulching and basin treatments, whose waterlogged plants had yellow leaves and stunted growth [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. In a Kenyan on-farm trial, ridged plots with fertiliser at the relatively wetter sub-humid Rachuonyo site gave the lowest yields, slightly below conventional practice, which the authors say can probably be explained by waterlogging caused by ridging [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: The pool is split: the literature units that show harm are tied to wet years or high-rainfall zones and give no magnitude or share of field affected, while more of the units, all WOCAT practitioner ratings, report better drainage; the Chinese check-dam and Indian farm-pond sheets rate it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_excess_water_drainage]. The Burkina Faso statements are cited rather than measured, and the Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors [ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. The meta-analysis figure is a share of observations, not an effect size [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_3]. The Ethiopian waterlogging finding is a field observation with no measured yield loss, and the source names a tillage treatment as the one particularly affected, so only part of the harm can be put on mulch and basins [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. The Kenyan ridging loss is the authors' probable explanation rather than a measured waterlogging contrast, and the ridging is bundled with fertiliser; because it comes from using the practice at a wetter site than it suits, it is held out of the production classes as an envelope misfit (a suitability caveat) and counted here as waterlogging evidence [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings, WOCAT compilers for water-harvesting works in Peru, Cabo Verde and Jordan rate drainage of excess water as improved, the Philippine conservation-tillage compiler rates it worse, and the Chinese check-dam sheet records no change [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner rating of drainage on a technology sheet, with no comment and no measured waterlogging or yield loss. The measured harm in the wider pool, in-field capture that waterlogged crops in wet years or high-rainfall zones, comes mostly from low- and lower-middle-income settings and is not in this scope, so this row says only that these structures were judged to drain well where they were documented.

water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced for terraces in Rwanda and Haiti, stone lines in Tunisia, check dams in India, micro water harvesting in Jordan and stone lines, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia, the Somali compiler noting the structures stabilised the landscape and reduced damage from intense rainfall and stormwater runoff [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_1553_2012_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.conditionality: The class follows the sub-practice vote, which tempers the pooled result: check dams in India and stone lines, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia hold the stronger ratings, while terraces in Rwanda and Haiti and stone lines in Tunisia hold the weaker ones, and the NbS-level class follows the terracing side [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_1553_2012_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. The Jordan micro water harvesting rating and the Ethiopian rating of unchanged storm impacts come from sub-practices with no family row of their own in this cell, so they count toward agreement but do not vote [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. Every unit is a WOCAT compiler rating with no measurement, and the ratings concern rain-storm damage more than wind; the Haiti compiler says the impact is not yet measured [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. The Ethiopian compiler rates storm impacts as unchanged [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.conditionality: This rests on a single practitioner rating with no stated reasoning, and the compilers for conservation tillage in the Philippines and stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde rate wind velocity as unchanged [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1021_2011_wind_velocity, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1573_2013_wind_velocity].
